you, servants of god, are upon a this-worldly path which is a representation of the path of the hereafter. you know that the path of the hereafter has upon it hooks like the thorns of the saʿdān plant, and that people differ upon it according to their deeds. so likewise this this-worldly path, the white clear way, has upon it hooks that catch hold of people; whoever is not steadfast upon it will turn away upon his heels. god, exalted be he, said: {and among people is he who worships god upon an edge. if good befalls him he is at ease with it, and if a trial befalls him he turns about upon his face. he has lost this world and the hereafter. that is the manifest loss} (sūrat al-ḥajj 22:11).

likewise, among the means of steadfastness in this religion is not to be hasty in a person's attaining his reward in this life. the reward of god, glorified and exalted, is what he has prepared for his friends in the abode of lasting bliss. that reward is god's bringing his friends near, mighty and majestic is he, and his choosing them — when god whitens their faces, gives them their books in their right hands, places them in the first company, brings them near in the highest firdaws of the garden, and shades them with the shade of his throne on a day when there is no shade but his shade; for he has chosen them for that.

therefore a person must be eager for the reward of the hereafter, and must know that what is hastened to him in this life is only a diminishing of his reward. it is established as sound (ṣaḥīḥ) from the prophet, god bless him and grant him peace, that he said: "no raiding party goes out in the path of god and takes spoils but that two thirds of its reward has been hastened to it; and no raiding party goes out in the path of god and fails but that it attains its reward in full."

therefore we must be eager, servants of god, that the hereafter be the bulk of our concern, and that we be eager for the reward of the hereafter, and that we not be eager to hasten anything of our reward in this life.

then know — may god have mercy on me and on you — that those to whom something is hastened in this life, even if they are among the best of the friends of god, always remain in wariness and fear. for that reason al-bukhari and muslim reported in the two ṣaḥīḥ collections from abd al-rahman ibn awf, may god be pleased with him, that he was fasting, and the table was set before him, and there were on it various kinds of food, and he wept a severe weeping until he made those around him weep. they said: "abu al-mundhir, what makes you weep?" he said: "we were a people of ignorance and evil, and god sent to us his messenger, god bless him and grant him peace, and we believed and affirmed the truth and followed. among us are those who died and did not have anything of their reward hastened to them — among them my brother musab ibn umayr, who was killed on the day of uhud and had nothing but his sword and a cloak upon him: if we covered his head with it his feet showed, and if we covered his feet his head showed. so the messenger of god, god bless him and grant him peace, ordered us to cover his head and to put some idhkhir grass over his feet. so he died and had nothing of his reward hastened to him. and we remained after them, and this world opened its doors to us and we gather its fruit; so we fear that it may be said to us on the day of resurrection: {you used up your good things in your worldly life and took your enjoyment of them. so today you are recompensed with the punishment of humiliation for having been arrogant in the earth without right, and for having been rebellious} (sūrat al-aḥqāf 46:20)."

the like of this is established as sound from khabbab ibn al-aratt, may god be pleased with him.

and it is established that the prophet, god bless him and grant him peace, went out of his house — nothing brought him out but hunger — and he met abu bakr and umar and said: "what has brought the two of you out of your houses?" they said: "hunger has brought us out." he said: "and i — nothing has brought me out but hunger." so they went to abu al-haytham ibn al-tayyihan, and he received them as guests. when he took his knife, intending to slaughter a sheep, the prophet, god bless him and grant him peace, forbade him the milk-bearing ones, that is, the milch animals. and when he set before them a cluster of dates and meat and cool water, the prophet, god bless him and grant him peace, looked at that and said: "this is among the bounty you will be asked about." {then you will certainly be asked on that day about the bounty} (sūrat al-takāthur 102:8).

it is upon us, servants of god, to beware of being among those whose rewards are hastened to them in this life, so that they reap them in matters that are cut off and in which there is no benefit. those people are worth nothing with god, for their worth is what god hastens to them of the matters of this perishing world.

then know — may god have mercy on me and on you — that among the means of uprightness and steadfastness in religion is that we remember that haste in obtaining the matters of this world is likewise a fault and a harm. al-bukhari reported in the ṣaḥīḥ from the report of khabbab ibn al-aratt, may god be pleased with him, that the prophet, god bless him and grant him peace, was reclining upon a cloak of his in the shade of the kaʿbah. khabbab said: i came to him and said: "messenger of god, will you not seek victory for us? will you not supplicate for us?" he said: "among those before you a man would be brought and the saw would be placed upon the parting of his head and he would be split with it into two halves; then iron combs would be brought and he would be combed with them, what is below his bone of skin and flesh — and that would not turn him from his religion. and by him in whose hand is the soul of muhammad, god will surely bring this affair to completion, until a rider travels from sanaa to hadramawt fearing none but god, and the wolf for his sheep. but you are a people who are hasty."

so the prophet, god bless him and grant him peace, warned with an eloquent warning against this haste, and made clear its harm and its danger, and made clear that the future belongs to this religion inevitably, and that god will grant it victory and give it might, by the might of one who is mighty or by the abasement of one who is abased.

but whoever misses that opening, it is better for him. for the prophet, god bless him and grant him peace — god gave him the treasures of chosroes and caesar, yet god took him before he attained anything of that; they were opened to his companions after him and they spent them in the path of god. this is evidence that whoever misses the opening, it is better for him. and those who died before the opening are the ones who were true to what they had covenanted with god. for the prophet, god bless him and grant him peace, eight days before his death, stood over the martyrs of uhud and said: "i am a witness over these, that they were true to god in what they covenanted with him."

and you know that the prophet, god bless him and grant him peace, was taken by god without having eaten his fill for three consecutive days, and three months would pass in which no fire was seen in his houses. he used to sleep upon a reed mat and it would leave its mark in his side — may my father and mother be his ransom, god bless him and grant him peace.

then know — may god have mercy on me and on you — that among the means of steadfastness upon this arduous road is that a person should remember the stories of those who went before and preceded him upon the road, and what they met with of harm in the path of god. let us remember, my brothers, how people used to mock noah, peace be upon him. and let us remember the conspiring together of the nearest kin against abraham when they cast him into the fire, and let us remember their expelling him from their city. and let us remember likewise what lot met with from his people. and let us remember what the prophets met with after that, down to our prophet muhammad, god bless him and grant him peace, of harm in the path of god, and what his companions met with of harm.

for the prophet, god bless him and grant him peace, was prostrating to his lord at the yemeni corner, and uqbah ibn abi muayt came and put his foot upon the nape of the messenger of god, god bless him and grant him peace — that is, the back of his head — and uqbah was heavy and fat, and he kept pressing him with his foot, until he ordered one who came to him with the afterbirth of a she-camel that had given birth, and placed it between his shoulders while he was prostrating to his lord.

and likewise nawfal bound abu bakr and talha ibn ubayd allah together with a leather thong and struck them upon their cheeks a severe striking until he made their cheeks bleed.

and likewise a number of the companions of the messenger of god, god bless him and grant him peace, were harmed with severe harm, in addition to what they met with of other pressures. thus sad ibn abi waqqas, when he accepted islam and made his islam public, his mother went on hunger strike and swore that she would not eat and would not drink until he turned back from his religion. when he feared death for her, he whispered in her ear and said: "mother, if you had a hundred souls, and they went out one soul after another, on condition that i turn back from my religion, i would not turn back from it. so live or die."

therefore we must know that we are being tested by this religion, and that we are in need of steadfastness in it; in need of knowing that whoever is not steadfast in his religion harms none but himself, and does not harm god or his religion in anything; and that this religion continues until god inherits the earth and whoever is upon it.

then know likewise — may god have mercy on me and on you — that whoever remembers the stories of those who have passed and the condition they were in will always expect to meet with some of what they met with, according to his degree in faith and god-consciousness. for you are travelling a road which those pioneers who went before travelled, and you are not nobler in the sight of god than they were; so what they met with, you must inevitably receive your share of it. god, exalted be he, says: {in the name of god, the merciful, the compassionate. alif lām mīm. do people reckon that they will be left to say "we believe" and not be tried? we tried those before them, and god will surely know those who are truthful and will surely know the liars} (sūrat al-ʿankabūt 29:1–3).

may god bless me and you in the mighty qur'an, and may he benefit me and you by what is in it of verses and wise remembrance. and may he turn in forgiveness to me and to you; he is the ever-relenting, the merciful.

praise belongs to god for his beneficence, and thanks be to him for his favour and his bounty. i bear witness that there is no god but god alone, having no partner, in magnification of his affair; and i bear witness that muhammad is his servant and his messenger, the one who calls to his good pleasure — god bless him and his family, his companions, his wives, his offspring and his brethren, and grant them peace.

servants of god, among the means of steadfastness in the religion of god is that a person should read the stories of the prophets in the qur'an. it is established as sound from abd allah ibn al-mubarak, may god be pleased with him, that he said: "the stories of the righteous are a host among the hosts of god, by which god makes firm the hearts of his servants." the confirmation of that from the qur'an is the words of god, exalted be he: {and all that we relate to you of the tidings of the messengers is that by which we make your heart firm. and there has come to you in this the truth, and an admonition and a reminder for the believers} (sūrat hūd 11:120).

so it is upon us, servants of god, to remember what they were in and what they were harmed with in the path of god, and to know that the road is long, and that ahead of us is more than what we have met with, and that there remains of the road more than has passed.

therefore know — may god have mercy on me and on you — that it is upon you to expect more trial for the religion of god, whether that be through adversity or through ease; and to know that not one of you has any guarantee of steadfastness in the religion of god, except whomever god, mighty and majestic, makes firm.

then know likewise — may god have mercy on me and on you — that among the means of steadfastness in the religion of god is holding to the congregation (jamāʿah). for the prophet, god bless him and grant him peace, said: "the hand of god is with the congregation, and whoever separates himself separates himself into the fire." and he said: "the hand of god is over the congregation, and the wolf eats only the sheep that strays far off." and he said: "whoever parts from the congregation by a handspan dies a death of ignorance." and he said: "whoever parts from the congregation has cast off the collar of islam from his neck." and he said to hudhayfah: "you are to hold to the congregation of the muslims and their imam." and he said: "the blood of a muslim man is not lawful except by one of three: the married fornicator, a life for a life, and one who abandons his religion, parting from the congregation."

that is because the believer, when he is with his brothers, will feel shame before many matters; and his being in their midst will be a making-firm of him upon the truth; and he will likewise be open to being counselled if some lapse proceeds from him. sincere counsel is part of the reminder, and the reminder benefits the believers. but he who cuts himself off from counsel, and finds no one to direct him in his state of weakness and no one to help him against his devil and his own soul in the state of weakness, is exposed to reversing upon his heels.

then know likewise — may god have mercy on me and on you — that among the means of steadfastness in this religion is that a person should remember his responsibility. for we are now in a time in which we hold the banner of islam; people have drawn back from it and left it in your hands, and god, glorified and exalted, has no need of you. so show god good from yourselves, and know that you attained this great honouring by god's granting of success and his choice, not of your own accord. therefore you must stand fast upon it and be patient.

then know likewise — may god have mercy on me and on you — that among the means of steadfastness and uprightness upon this road is that a person should remember those behind him who look to his conduct: if he is upright they are upright, and if he is crooked they are crooked. they hang their hopes upon you, and they look to your patience upon the road. you are their teachers and the ones taken as models upon the road of uprightness. so if you are patient, the people behind you are patient.

ibn abbas, may god be pleased with them both, said: "i grieved at the parting from al-abbas ibn abd al-muttalib, and nothing made me firm except a bedouin who said:

*be patient, and we shall be patient through you, for the patience of the flock is at the patience of the head. / better than al-abbas is your reward after him, and god is better for al-abbas than you.*"

then, among the means of steadfastness likewise and of uprightness upon this road, is that a person should remember what god has prepared for those steadfast upon it of establishment in the life of this world and of being brought near in the hereafter. for those who were steadfast upon this road, even if they were killed upon it, are the ones whom god establishes, and establishes for them by love in the hearts of the servants of god.

do you not see that those who were killed on the day of uhud — god has given them acceptance in the souls of all the believers, and they do not cease to be attached to them and to take them as models and to love them with the utmost love? this is establishment. for establishment is only in the hearts of the people of faith and the people of god, mighty and majestic. as for what is other than that, it is all passing away and cut off.

and those who were killed on the day of uhud and those who escaped and lived have all alike come to their end. the hypocrites who turned back from the messenger of god, god bless him and grant him peace, with half the army when they faced the idolaters on the day of uhud did not live on to this time of ours, and attained nothing but their allotted provisions which had been written for them, and their lifespans were not increased by anything, and they had no standing whatever; god did not write good for them, neither in this world nor in the hereafter.

and those who stood fast and were patient — among them abd allah ibn amr ibn haram: when the hypocrites turned back from the messenger of god, god bless him and grant him peace, he stood over them and said: "o my people, do not forsake the messenger of god, god bless him and grant him peace, in this position; perhaps it will not happen again that you are called to the defence while you are able to it." they said: "if we knew there would be fighting we would have followed you." so he turned back and said: "may god disgrace you, and god will make his messenger, god bless him and grant him peace, independent of you." then he went down and fought until he was killed, and he entered the garden. god offered him that he might wish for whatever he wished, and he wished that he would return him to life so that he might fight and be killed in the path of god a second time.

he was taken out of his grave after forty-six years. jabir said: while i was in the mosque, a caller came to me and said: "your father has been taken out of his grave." so i went out running hard to the martyrs, and there were sixteen of the ansar who had been taken out of their graves — and that was in the days of muawiyah ibn abi sufyan, may god be pleased with them both — and their wounds were flowing with blood. he said: i lifted the hand of one of them from his flank and the blood came out; and his hand returned and the blood was stilled.

they are the ones about whom god sent down: {and do not reckon those who were killed in the path of god as dead. rather they are living with their lord, provided for, rejoicing in what god has given them of his bounty, and receiving good tidings concerning those who have not yet joined them from behind them, that there shall be no fear upon them nor shall they grieve. they receive good tidings of a blessing from god and a bounty, and that god does not let the reward of the believers go to waste — those who responded to god and the messenger after the wound had afflicted them. for those of them who did good and were god-conscious there is a great reward. those to whom people said: the people have gathered against you, so fear them — and it increased them in faith and they said: god is sufficient for us, and an excellent guardian is he. so they returned with a blessing from god and a bounty; no evil touched them, and they followed the good pleasure of god; and god is possessed of great bounty} (sūrat āl ʿimrān 3:169–174).

likewise, among the means of steadfastness in the religion of god is that a person be eager for uprightness upon this road in his times of solitude: that when he is alone with himself he be among those who remember god much, and that he be eager in his solitude to show god good from himself. for god, glorified and exalted, is ever watchful over his servants; no thought passes in the heart of a person, and his eye does not cast a glance, but that it is recorded and written with god, mighty and majestic.

therefore the believer who travels this road must be conscious of god's watching over him, glorified and exalted, and that he is nearer to him than the jugular vein, and that all his deeds are laid before him and he will read them when he is called before the assembled witnesses: {read your book. sufficient is your own self against you this day as a reckoner} (sūrat al-isrāʾ 17:14).

likewise, among the means of steadfastness in the religion of god is that a person strive in supplication that god make him firm upon the road of uprightness. the prophet, god bless him and grant him peace, used often to say: "o god, turner of hearts, make our hearts firm upon your religion." "o god, disposer of hearts, dispose our hearts to your obedience."

the prophet, god bless him and grant him peace — though he is protected from sin, and god had forgiven him what went before of his fault and what came after — used to be eager to say this supplication often. is it not then fitting for the believer who travels his road to be eager to say this supplication often and to take provision from it, knowing that at every moment he is exposed to god's turning him about, mighty and majestic? we ask god for steadfastness and uprightness upon his road.

god, mighty and majestic, says: {god makes firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the hereafter; and god leads the wrongdoers astray; and god does what he wills} (sūrat ibrāhīm 14:27).

servants of god, god has commanded you with a command in which he began with himself, and made his angels second in it, and made you, company of believers, third. he said — and noble is he who speaks: {indeed god and his angels send blessings upon the prophet. o you who believe, send blessings upon him and greet him with peace} (sūrat al-aḥzāb 33:56).

o god, bless and grant peace and increase and blessing to our prophet muhammad, your servant, your prophet and your messenger, the unlettered prophet, and to his family and his companions, and grant them peace.

o god, give might to islam and the muslims, and abase associating partners with god (shirk) and those who associate partners with him. weaken the scheming of the unbelievers and grant us victory over them all. o god, make your religion and your book prevail over all religion, though those who associate partners with god be averse.

o god, succeed muhammad, god bless him and grant him peace, in his community with good. o god, grant us to hold fast to his sunnah when his community is corrupted. gather us under his banner and raise us in his company. give us to drink from his pool, by his noble hand, a pleasant draught after which we shall never thirst again. whiten our faces on the day when faces are whitened and faces are blackened. give us our books in our right hands, before our faces, and bring us across the path like flashing lightning, o most merciful of the merciful.

o god, we ask you by your noble face for the highest firdaws of the garden. o god, we ask you by your noble face for the highest firdaws of the garden.

o god, whoever intends evil against us or against islam, occupy him with himself, make his scheming his own destruction, turn the turn of evil upon him, send down upon him exemplary punishments, and send down upon him your might which is not turned back from the criminal people; and show us in him the wonders of your power, soon and without delay — you have power over all things.

servants of god: {indeed god commands justice and excellence and giving to kinsfolk, and he forbids indecency and wrong and oppression. he admonishes you, that you may take heed} (sūrat al-naḥl 16:90). so remember god, the mighty, the majestic, and he will remember you; and thank him for his blessings with a true thankfulness, and he will increase you. and the remembrance of god is greater, and god knows what you do.
r: إن الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينه ، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا ومن سيئات أعمالنا من يهده الله فلا مضل له ومن يضلل فلا هادي له ، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له وأشهد أن محمدا عبده ورسوله صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وأصحابه وسلم تسليما كثيرا (يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اتَّقُوا رَبَّكُمُ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ نَفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ وَخَلَقَ مِنْهَا زَوْجَهَا وَبَثَّ مِنْهُمَا رِجَالًا كَثِيرًا وَنِسَاءً وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ الَّذِي تَسَاءَلُونَ بِهِ وَالْأَرْحَامَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَلَيْكُمْ رَقِيبًا) (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آَمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَقُولُوا قَوْلًا سَدِيدًا (70) يُصْلِحْ لَكُمْ أَعْمَالَكُمْ وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ ذُنُوبَكُمْ وَمَنْ يُطِعِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ فَقَدْ فَازَ فَوْزًا عَظِيمًا) أما بعد، فإن خير الحديث كتاب الله وخير الهدي هدي محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وشر الأمور محدثاتها وكل بدعة ضلالة ، عباد الله إن الله سبحانه وتعالى يهدي من يشاء إلى صراطه المستقيم ، ويثبت من أراد ثباته على ذلك الصراط ، ويمتحن الناس ويبتليهم عليه ، ومن أراد الله ثباته فإنه سيثبت وقد أمر الله سبحانه وتعالى بالأخذ بالأسباب في كل الأمور ومن ذلك أسباب الهداية والاستقامة ، فمن أسباب الهداية تعلم ما أمر الله به والعمل بما جاء به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم والاقتداء بالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في الأقوال والأعمال والاعتقادات والنيات ، ومن أسباب الهداية كذلك الضراعة إلى الله سبحانه وتعالى بسؤال الهداية ومن أسباب الهداية التدبر والتذكر ، ثم بعد ذلك أسباب الثبات على دين الله وهي أعظم وأولى باشتغال المسلم بها ، فمن أعظمها أن يتذكر المسلم أنه في هذه الحياة في سنة التدافع وفي جدلية لا بد فيها من الحسم ، وهذه الجدلية هي الاستقامة على طريق الهداية إلى الموت أو الرجوع والإنقلاب على عقبيه ، فالناس قسمان إما أن يكون الإنسان من الأتقياء وإما أن يكون من الأشقياء ، فالأتقياء هم السعداء الذين يثبتهم الله بالقول الثابت في الحياة الدنيا وفي الآخرة ، وإذا عرف الإنسان هذه الجدلية وعرف انقسام الناس إلى القسمين ، وعرف أن ذلك لا يكون بنسب ولا حسب وإنما يكون بأخذ الأسباب وباختيار الملك الديان سبحانه وتعالى حرص على أن لا يكون من الأشقياء وعلى أن يكون من أهل الهداية وأن يلزم ذلك طيلة حياته ، ثم من أسباب الاستقامة و الثبات كذلك أن يعلم الإنسان طول هذا الطريق وما عليه من المشاق ، فإن كثيرا من الناس يرجعون عند أول نكبة ويتراجعون عن طريق الاستقامة والهداية ولا يصمدون عليه ولا يثبتون لأنهم يجهلون ما عليه من النكبات والعقبات وأنتم عباد الله على صراط دنيوي هو تمثيل للصراط الأخروي وتعرفون أن الصراط الأخروي عليه كلاليب كشوك السعدان ، يتفاوت الناس عليه بحسب أعمالهم ، فكذلك هذا الصراط الدنيوي المحجة البيضاء عليه كلاليب تمسك بالناس ، فمن لم يثبت عليه فإنه سينصرف على عقبيه ، وقد قال الله تعالى: (ومن الناس من يعبد الله على حرف فإن أصابه خير اطمأن به وإن أصابته فتنة انقلب على وجهه خسر الدنيا والآخرة ذلك هو الخسران المبين) كذلك من وسائل الثبات على هذا الدين عدم الاستعجال في أن ينال الإنسان الثواب في هذه الحياة ، فثواب الله سبحانه و تعالى هو ما أعده لأوليائه في دار النعيم المقيم ، إن ذلك الثواب هو تقريب الله عز وجل لأوليائه واصطفاؤه لهم ، إذا بيض الله وجوههم وآتاهم كتبهم بأيمانهم وجعلهم في الزمرة الأولى وقربهم في الفردوس الأعلى من الجنة وأظلهم بظل عرشه يوم لا ظل إلا ظله فإنه قد اختارهم لذلك فلذلك لا بد أن يحرص الإنسان على الثواب الأخروي ، وأن يعلم أن ما يعجل له في هذه الحياة إنما هو نقص من أجره ، فقد صح عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: \"ما من سرية تخرج في سبيل الله فتغنم إلا عجل لها ثلثا أجرها وما من سرية تخرج في سبيل الله فتخفق إلا نالت أجرها كاملا\" فلذلك لا بد أن نحرص عباد الله على أن تكون الآخرة جل اهتمامنا وأن نحرص على الثواب الأخروي وأن لا نحرص على تعجل شيء من ثوابنا في هذه الحياة ، ثم اعلموا رحمني الله وإياكم أن الذين يعجل لهم شيء في هذه الحياة حتى لو كانوا من خيرة أولياء الله فإنهم دائما يبقون على حذر وخوف ، ولذلك أخرج البخاري ومسلم في الصحيحين عن عبد الرحمن بن عوف رضي الله عنه أنه كان صائما فوضعت المائدة بين يديه فإذا فيها ألوانا من الطعام فبكى بكاء شديدا حتى أبكى من حوله ، فقالوا يا أبا المنذر وما يبكيك قال إنا كنا أهل جاهلية وشر فأرسل الله إلينا رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم فآمنا وصدقنا واتبعنا فمنا من مات ولم يتعجل شيئا من أجره ، منهم أخي مصعب بن عمير قتل يوم أحد وليس له إلا سيفه وبردة عليه إن نحن غطينا بها رأسه بدت رجلاه وإن نحن غطينا رجليه بدا رأسه فأمرنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن نغطي رأسه وأن نجعل على رجليه من الإذخر فمات ولم يتعجل شيئا من أجره وبقينا وراءهم ففتحت علينا الدنيا أبوابها فنحن نهدبها فخشينا أن يقال لنا يوم القيامة: (أذهبتم طيباتكم في حياتكم الدنيا واستمتعتم بها فاليوم تجزون عذاب الهون بما كنتم تستكبرون في الأرض بغير الحق وبما كنتم تفسقون) وقد صح نظير هذا عن خباب بن الأرت رضي الله عنه وقد ثبت أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم خرج من بيته لا يخرجه إلا الجوع فلقي أبا بكر وعمر فقال ما أخرجكما من بيوتكما قالا الجوع أخرجنا ، قال وأنا ما أخرجني إلا الجوع ، فذهبوا إلى أبي الهيثم بن التيهان فضيفهما فلما أخذ مديته يريد أن يذبح شاة نهاه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن ذوات الدر أي الحلوب فلما وضع بين أيديهما عذقا من التمر ولحما وماء باردا نظر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى ذلك وقال: إن هذا من النعيم الذي تسألون عنه (ثم لتسألن يومئذ عن النعيم) إن علينا عباد الله أن نحذر أن نكون من الذين تعجل لهم أجورهم في هذه الحياة فيجنونها في أمور منقطعة لا فائدة فيها ، وإن أولئك لا يساوون عند الله شيئا فقيمتهم هي ما يعجله الله لهم من أمور هذه الدنيا الفانية ، ثم اعلموا رحمني الله وإياكم أن من وسائل الاستقامة والثبات على الدين أن نتذكر أن الاستعجال كذلك في تحصيل أمور هذه الدنيا عيب وضرر فقد أخرج البخاري في الصحيح من حديث خباب بن الأرت رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان متوسدا بردة له في ظل الكعبة قال خباب فأتيته فقلت يا رسول الله ألا تستنصر لنا ألا تدعو لنا ، فقال: إنه قد كان فيمن قبلكم يؤتى بالرجل فيوضع المنشار على مفرقه فيفرق به فرقتين ثم يؤتى بأمشاط الحديد فيمشط بها ما دون عظمه من جلد ولحم لا يصده ذلك عن دينه و والذي نفس محمد بيده ليتمن الله هذا الأمر حتى يسير الراكب من صنعاء إلى حضرموت لا يخاف إلا الله والذئب على غنمه ولكنكم قوم تستعجلون\" فحذر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم تحذيرا بليغا من هذا الاستعجال وبين ضرره وخطره وبين أن المستقبل لهذا الدين لا محالة وأن الله سينصره ويعزه بعز عزيز أو بذل ذليل ، لكن من فاته ذلك الفتح فهو خير له فالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم آتاه الله كنوز كسرى وقيصر ولكنه توفاه الله قبل أن ينال شيئا من ذلك ، فتحت على أصحابه من بعده فأنفقوها في سبيل الله ، وهذا دليل على أن من فاته الفتح فهو خير له ، والذين ماتوا قبل الفتح هم الذين صدقوا ما عاهدوا الله عليه ، فالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قبل موته بثمانية أيام وقف على شهداء أحد فقال: \"إني شهيد على هؤلاء بأن صدقوا الله ما عاهدوه عليه\" وأنتم تعلمون أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم توفاه الله ولم يشبع ثلاثة أيام متواليات ويمضي ثلاثة أشهر ما يرى في بيوته نار ، وقد كان ينام على الحصير فيؤثر في جنبه بأبي هو وأمي صلى الله عليه وسلم ثم اعلموا رحمني الله وإياكم أن من وسائل الثبات على هذا الطريق الشاق أن يتذكر الإنسان قصص السالفين السابقين الذين سلكوا الطريق من قبله وما لقوه من الأذى في سبيل الله فلنتذكر إخواني ما كان الناس يسخرون به من نوح عليه السلام ، ولنتذكر تمالُؤ الأقربين على إبراهيم حين رموه في النار ولنتذكر إخراجهم له من مدينتهم ولنتذكر كذلك ما لقي لوط من قومه ولنتذكر ما لقي النبيون من بعد ذلك إلى نبينا محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم من الأذى في سبيل الله وما لقيه أصحابه من الأذى ، فإن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان ساجدا لربه عند الركن اليماني فجاء عقبة بن أبي معيط فوضع رجله على قذال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أي مؤخرة رأسه وكان عقبة ثقيلا سمينا فما زال يدعه برجله حتى أمر من أتاه بسلا ناقة ولدت فوضعه بين كتفيه وهو ساجد لربه ، وكذلك فإن نوفلا قرن أبا بكر وطلحة بن عبيد الله بنسع وضربهما على خديهما ضربا شديدا حتى أدما خديهما ، وكذلك فإن عددا من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أوذوا أذى شديدا بالإضافة إلى ما لقوا من الضغوط الأخرى ، فهذا سعد بن أبي وقاص عندما أسلم وأشهر إسلامه أضربت أمه عن الطعام ، فأقسمت أن لا تأكل وأن لا تشرب حتى يرجع عن دينه ، فلما خشي عليها الموت همس في أذنها فقال يا أماه لو كان لك مائة نفس فخرجت نفسا تلو أخرى على أن أرجع عن ديني ما رجعت عنه ، فاحيي أو فموتي... فلذلك لا بد أن نعلم أننا ممتحنون بهذا الدين وأننا محتاجون إلى الثبات عليه ، محتاجون إلى أن نعلم أن من لم يثبت على دينه لا يضر إلا نفسه ولا يضر الله ودينه شيئا وأن هذا الدين مستمر إلى أن يرث الله الأرض ومن عليها ثم اعلموا رحمني الله وإياكم كذلك أن الذي يتذكر قصص الماضين وما هم عليه فإنه سيتوقع دائما أن ينال بعض ما نالهم بحسب درجته في الإيمان والتقوى ، فأنتم تسلكون طريقا سلكه أولئك الرائدون السابقون ولستم أكرم على الله منهم فما لقوه لا بد أن تنالوا حظكم منه يقول الله تعالى: (بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم ألم أحسب الناس أن يتركوا أن يقولوا آمنا وهم لا يفتنون ولقد فتنا الذين من قبلهم فليعلمن الله الذين صدقوا وليعلمن الكاذبين) بارك الله لي ولكم في القرآن العظيم ونفعني وإياكم بما فيه من الآيات والذكر الحكيم وتاب علي وعليكم إنه هو التواب الرحيم. الحمد لله على إحسانه والشكر له على تفضله وامتنانه وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له تعظيما لشانه وأشهد أن محمدا عبده ورسوله الداعي إلى رضوانه صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وأصحابه وأزواجه وذريته وإخوانه. عباد الله إن من وسائل الثبات على دين الله أن يقرأ الإنسان قصص الأنبياء في القرآن فقد صح عن عبد الله بن المبارك رضي الله عنه أنه قال: قصص الصالحين جند من جنود الله يثبت الله بها قلوب عباده ، ومصداق ذلك من القرآن قول الله تعالى: (وكلا نقص عليك من أنباء الرسل ما نثبت به فؤادك وجاءك في هذه الحق وموعظة وذكرى للمؤمنين) فعلينا عباد الله أن نتذكر ما كانوا فيه وما أوذوا به في سبيل الله وأن نعلم أن الطريق طويل وأن أمامنا أكثر مما لقينا وأن الطريق قد بقي منه أكثر مما مضى ، فلذلك اعلموا رحمني الله وإياكم أن عليكم أن تتوقعوا المزيد من الابتلاء على دين الله سواء كان ذلك بالضراء أو بالسراء ، وأن تعلموا أنه ليس لدى أحد منكم ضمان بالثبات على دين الله إلا من ثبته الله عز وجل ، ثم اعلموا رحمني الله وإياكم كذلك أن من وسائل الثبات على دين الله لزوم الجماعة ، فإن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: \"يد الله مع الجماعة ومن شذ شذ في النار\" وقال: \"يد الله على الجماعة وإنما يأكل الذئب من الغنم القاصية\" وقال: \"من فارق الجماعة شبرا مات ميتة جاهلية\" وقال: \"من فارق الجماعة فقد خلع ربقة الإسلام من عنقه\" وقال لحذيفة: \"تلزم جماعة المسلمين وإمامهم\" وقال: \"لا يحل دم امرئ مسلم إلا بإحدى ثلاث \"الثيب الزاني والنفس بالنفس والتارك لدينه المفارق للجماعة\" وذلك أن المؤمن إذا كان مع إخوانه فإنه سيستحي من كثير من الأمور ، وسيكون وجوده بين ظهرانيهم تثبيتا له على الحق ، وسيكون كذلك عرضة للمناصحة إذا بدرت منه بادرة ، والنصيحة هي من الذكرى والذكرى تنفع المؤمنين ، والذي ينقطع عن النصيحة ولا يجد من يوجهه في حال ضعفه ولا من يساعده على شيطانه ونفسه في حال الضعف عرضة للانقلاب على عقبيه ثم اعلموا رحمني الله وإياكم كذلك أن من أسباب الثبات على هذا الدين أن يتذكر الإنسان مسؤوليته ، فنحن الآن في وقت نمسك فيه بلواء الإسلام قد تراجع الناس عنه وتركوه في أيديكم والله سبحانه وتعالى غني عنكم فأروا الله من أنفسكم خيرا واعلموا أنكم نلتم هذا التشريف العظيم بتوفيق الله واختياره لا من تلقاء أنفسكم فلذلك لا بد أن تصمدوا عليه وتصبروا ثم اعلموا رحمني الله وإياكم كذلك أن من وسائل الثبات و الاستقامة على هذا الطريق أن يتذكر الإنسان من وراءه من الذين ينظرون إلى تصرفاته فإن استقام استقاموا وإن اعوج اعوجوا ، إنهم يعلقون عليكم الآمال وإنهم ينظرون إلى صبركم على الطريق فأنتم أساتذتهم والمقتدى بكم على طريق الاستقامة ، فإذا صبرتم صبر الناس من ورائكم وقد قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: لقد حزنت على فراق العباس بن عبد المطلب فما ثبتني إلا أعرابي قال: اصبر نكن بك صابرين فإنما صبر الرعية عند صبر الراس خير من العباس أجرك بعده والله خير منك للعباس ثم إنه من وسائل الثبات كذلك والاستقامة على هذا الطريق أن يتذكر الإنسان ما أعده الله للثابتين عليه من التمكين في الحياة الدنيا ومن التقريب في الآخرة فالذين ثبتوا على هذا الطريق ولو قتلوا عليه هم الذين يمكن الله لهم ويمكن لهم بالمحبة في قلوب عباد الله ، ألا ترون أن الذين قتلوا يوم أحد قد جعل الله لهم القبول في نفوس المؤمنين جميعا ، ولا يزالون يتعلقون بهم ويقتدون بهم ويحبونهم غاية المحبة ، وهذا هو التمكين ، فإن التمكين إنما يكون في قلوب أهل الإيمان وأهل الله عز وجل ، أما ما سوى ذلك فهو كله زائل منقطع والذين قتلوا يوم أحد والذين نجوا وعاشوا قد اداركوا جميعا ، فالمنافقون الذين رجعوا عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بنصف الجيش حين واجهوا المشركين يوم أحد لم يعمروا إلى زماننا هذا ولم ينالوا إلا أرزاقهم التي كتبت لهم ولم تزدد أعمارهم بشيء ، ولم يكن لهم أية مكانة ، فلم يكتب الله لهم الخير لا في الدنيا ولا في الآخرة ، والذين صمدوا وصبروا ومنهم عبد الله بن عمرو بن حرام حين رجع المنافقون عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وقف عليهم فقال: أي قومي لا تخذلوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في هذا الموقف فعسى أن لا يتكرر أن تدعوا إلى الدفع وأنتم قادرون عليه ، فقالوا: لو كنا نعلم قتالا لاتبعناكم ، فرجع وقال: أخزاكم الله وأغنى عنكم رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم فنزل فقاتل حتى قتل فدخل الجنة ، وعرض الله عليه أن يتمنى عليه ما شاء فتمنى أن يرده للحياة حتى يقاتل فيقتل في سبيل الله مرة أخرى ، وقد أخرج من قبره بعد ست و أربعين سنة قال جابر، بينا أنا في المسجد إذ جاءني مناد فقال: إن أباك قد أخرج من قبره فخرجت أشتد عدوا إلى الشهداء فإذا ستة عشر من الأنصار قد أخرجوا من قبورهم وذلك في أيام معاوية بن أبي سفيان رضي الله عنهما ، فإذا جراحهم تنزف بالدم ، قال فرفعت يد أحدهم عن خاصرته فخرج الدم ، فعادت يده فسكن الدم ، إنهم الذين أنزل الله فيهم: (ولا تحسبن الذين قتلوا في سبيل الله أمواتا بل أحياء عند ربهم يرزقون فرحين بما آتاهم الله من فضله ويستبشرون بالذين لم يلحقوا بهم من خلفهم أن لا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون يستبشرون بنعمة من الله وفضل وأن الله لا يضيع أجر المؤمنين الذين استجابوا لله والرسول من بعدما أصابهم القرح للذين أحسنوا منهم واتقوا أجر عظيم الذين قال لهم الناس إن الناس قد جمعوا لكم فاخشوهم فزادهم إيمانا وقالوا حسبنا الله ونعم الوكيل فانقلبوا بنعمة من الله وفضل لم يمسسهم سوء واتبعوا رضوان الله والله ذو فضل عظيم) كذلك من وسائل الثبات على دين الله أن يحرص الإنسان على الاستقامة على هذا الطريق في خلواته ، إذا خلى بنفسه أن يكون من الذاكرين الله كثيرا أن يحرص في خلواته على أن يري الله من نفسه خيرا ، فالله سبحانه وتعالى لعباده بالمرصاد ، وما تخطر في قلب إنسان خطرة ولا تنظر عينه نظرة إلا وهي مسجلة مكتوبة عند الله عز وجل ، فلذلك لا بد أن يستشعر المؤمن السالك لهذا الطريق مراقبة الله سبحانه وتعالى له وأنه أقرب إليه من حبل الوريد وأن أعماله جميعا معروضة عليه يقرأها عندما ينادى على رؤوس الأشهاد (اقرأ كتابك كفى بنفسك اليوم عليك حسيبا) كذلك فإن من وسائل الثبات على دين الله أن يجتهد الإنسان في الدعاء أن يثبته الله على طريق الاستقامة وقد كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يكثر أن يقول: \"اللهم يا مقلب القلوب ثبت قلوبنا على دينك\" \"اللهم يا مصرف القلوب صرف قلوبنا على طاعتك\" إن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو معصوم قد غفر الله له ما تقدم من ذنبه وما تأخر كان يحرص على الإكثار من هذا الدعاء ، أفليس جديرا بالمؤمن الذي سلك طريقه أن يحرص على الإكثار من هذا الدعاء وأن يتزود منه وهو يعلم أنه في كل وقت عرضة لأن يقلبه الله عز وجل نسأل الله الثبات والاستقامة على طريقه. يقول الله عز وجل (يثبت الله الذين آمنوا بالقول الثابت في الحياة الدنيا وفي الآخرة ويضل الله الظالمين ويفعل الله ما يشاء). عباد الله إن الله أمركم بأمر بدأ فيه بنفسه وثنى فيه بملائكته وثلث بكم معاشر المؤمنين فقال جل من قائل كريما: (إن الله وملائكته يصلون على النبي يا أيها الذين آمنوا صلوا عليه وسلموا تسليما). اللهم صل وسلم وزد وبارك على نبينا محمد عبدك ونبيك ورسولك النبي الأمي وعلى آله وصحبه وسلم تسليما. اللهم أعز الإسلام والمسلمين وأذل الشرك والمشركين وأوهن كيد الكافرين وانصرنا عليهم أجمعين ، اللهم أظهر دينك وكتابك على الدين كله ولو كره المشركون ، اللهم اخلف محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم في أمته بخير ، اللهم ارزقنا التمسك بسنته عند فساد أمته ، واحشرنا تحت لوائه وابعثنا في زمرته ، واسقنا من حوضه بيده الشريفة شربة هنيئة لا نظمأ بعدها أبدا ، وبيض وجوهنا يوم تبيض وجوه وتسود وجوه ، وآتنا كتبنا بأيماننا تلقاء وجوهنا وجوزنا على الصراط كالبرق الخاطف يا أرحم الراحمين ، اللهم إنا نسألك بوجهك الكريم الفردوس الأعلى من الجنة ، اللهم إنا نسألك بوجهك الكريم الفردوس الأعلى من الجنة ، اللهم من أرادنا أو أراد الإسلام بسوء فاشغله بنفسه واجعل تدبيره تدميره واجعل دائرة السوء عليه وأنزل به المثلات وأنزل به بأسك الذي لا يرد عن القوم المجرمين وأرنا فيه عجائب قدرتك عاجلا غير رائث إنك على كل شيء قدير. عباد الله (إن الله يأمر بالعدل والإحسان وإيتاء ذي القربى وينهى عن الفحشاء والمنكر والبغي يعظكم لعلكم تذكرون) فاذكروا الله العظيم الجليل يذكركم واشكروه على نعمه شكرا حقيقيا يزدكم ، ولذكر الله أكبر والله يعلم ما تصنعون.

t: Balance and Moderation in the Life of the Muslim
a: التوازن والاعتدال في حياة المسلم
b:
in the name of god, the merciful, the compassionate. praise belongs to god, lord of the worlds. i pray for blessing and peace upon him who was sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his companions and whoever is guided by his guidance and takes his sunnah as his way until the day of judgement. peace be upon you, and the mercy of god and his blessings.

to proceed: god, glorified and exalted, created people upon his innate constitution (fiṭrah) which he approved, and that is servanthood to god, glorified and exalted, and fulfilling his right, and striving for what is beneficial and being eager for what avoids harm. this innate constitution is the condition of the sound and upright human being. whatever is other than it must be a swerving from this road, inclining to the right or to the left; and this inclining is what is called deviation, and it is what is called extremism away from the road of truth — that is, inclining away from the road of truth to the right or to the left.

this truth which god, exalted be he, approved for his servants — he sent his messengers with it and set it out with the most complete setting-out and sent down his books with it and established the proofs and evidences for it. it is protected from error and firmly fixed, and most of it, and the core of it, are clear matters upon which no two differ. what is other than that within it consists of matters open to independent legal reasoning (ijtihād), in which god, exalted be he, makes people's seeking of the truth an act of worship; so he grants success in reaching the truth in his sight to whomever he wills.

but all of them, if they sought the truth and were sincere to god, glorified and exalted, are excused — the one among them who was right and the one who erred. the one who is right among them has two rewards, and the one who errs has one reward, as is established as sound (ṣaḥīḥ) from the prophet, god bless him and grant him peace, that he said: "when the judge exercises independent legal reasoning and is right, he has two rewards; and when he exercises independent legal reasoning and errs, he has one reward."

so everyone who sought the truth and desired the face of god, glorified and exalted, in matters open to independent reasoning that are not settled by an explicit text, is excused, whether he reached the truth or erred. his having reached the truth is shown only by his agreeing with the proof and the evidence that comes from god, glorified and exalted — which may be hidden from a person in itself, so that knowledge of it does not reach him, because many of the proofs and evidences are not definitive in their transmission, such as singly transmitted reports and the like; or their indication may be hidden from him, as in the case of texts definitive in transmission, as is so in the qur'an, while not being definitive in indication. so at that point a person is excused if he did not comprehend it and did not understand it correctly.

for god, glorified and exalted, is able to set it out with the utmost clarity, as he set out other rulings; and he placed in it that hiddenness and that unelaborated character only for a wisdom that god, glorified and exalted, knows. among his wisdom in that is that he tests his servants with seeking the truth and searching for it, and with employing the intellects and the instruments with which he equipped them for understanding his book and for receiving from him, glorified and exalted.

it cannot be that god, glorified and exalted, should make part of the qur'an ambiguous, and part of it unelaborated, and part of it problematic, and part of it hidden in its indication — and then make it an act of worship binding upon all to arrive at a single path, namely the correct one. rather, it must follow from that hiddenness that god, glorified and exalted, grants the understanding of it as a provision to whomever he wills of the elect of his creation, and that he excuses whoever does not arrive at that — because the hiddenness in it is sufficient for excusing, and sufficient for the seeking and searching out of the truth.

and if a person exerts his effort, god, glorified and exalted, does not charge him with more than his effort; and he has stated this explicitly in his book in a number of verses. he, exalted be he, said: {god does not charge a soul except [with] its capacity} (sūrat al-baqarah 2:286) [the source's wording differs here; see flags]. and he, exalted be he, said: {god does not charge a soul except with what he has given it} (sūrat al-ṭalāq 65:7).

so it is upon a person to exert his effort in arriving at what is correct. if he arrives at it, then well and good: he has attained the conviction that this is what god intends, and has known its proof, so at that point it becomes binding upon him. and if he does not arrive at what is correct, but only arrives at what he himself is convinced is the nearest of the matters to god's good pleasure and the most fitting to be the truth — although it is capable of being a mistake — then at that point he is excused, like the state of the imams who exercised independent reasoning.

the imam malik, may god have mercy on him, used to say concerning this kind of derived question: {we only suppose a supposition, and we are not certain} (sūrat al-jāthiyah 45:32). and al-shafi'i, may god have mercy on him, used to say concerning it: "my opinion is correct with the possibility of being wrong, and another's opinion is wrong with the possibility of being correct."

and many of the eminent imams, in such matters open to independent reasoning, would exert their efforts and then pray the prayer for seeking guidance and ask god, glorified and exalted, to choose the good for them, and would disavow to god their own power and strength, depending and relying upon god alone.

this aspect of god-centredness is indispensable among the later generations, and it is absent in many of them except those upon whom god has had mercy. many of those who dispute over questions do not resort to appealing to god, glorified and exalted, that he make clear to them what is correct.

many of the eminent imams, men of intelligence and knowledge and experience, when a new case was presented to them, would be overcome by a sweat of anguish — as was the state of malik, may god have mercy on him: when he was asked about a question he would fall silent and remain long in gloom and cast his eyes to the ground, and the sweat would run down his face from the severity of the dread, because he knew that he was signing on behalf of the lord of the worlds and that he would answer for a question that would be put before him in the presence of the sovereign, the judge, and it would be said: "you gave a legal opinion of such-and-such." for that reason they strove in god-centredness and in appealing to god.

among the renowned for intelligence is ahmad ibn abd al-halim ibn taymiyyah, the shaykh of islam. when a question was presented to him he would pray two units of prayer and then sit in his place of prayer, bowed upon his knees, saying: "o teacher of david, teach me; and o giver of understanding to solomon, give me understanding."

so they appeal to god, exalted be he, to give them understanding of the truth. and this is very far from bigotry, and very far from a person's monopolising the truth and holding that the truth is only what he has and that what is other than it is falsehood itself.

therefore we must all take on the character of the scholars and their guidance, and must know that what god, glorified and exalted, has kept hidden of the questions is a provision which he provides to whomever he wills of his servants; and it is like other matters which require appealing to god and relying upon him and depending upon him in the whole affair.

and likewise a person must realise that he is weak. for just as his powers are too weak to fulfil god's right in his acts of worship — and not one of us is satisfied with any act of worship he has performed. is any one of you satisfied with the prayer he has just prayed, which is the afternoon prayer, the witnessed prayer, which many of the people of knowledge have said is the middle prayer? not one of you is able to be satisfied with his own work.

so he ought to realise that his understanding and his independent reasoning and his knowledge are part of his work, and so are not to be a source of self-satisfaction. for self-satisfaction with it is among the marks of hypocrisy: if a person is satisfied with his own knowledge and his own understanding, this is among the marks of hypocrisy. therefore he must realise that his knowledge is part of his work: just as his work falls short in all matters, so likewise do his knowledge and his understanding. by this he humbles himself before god, glorified and exalted, and becomes fit to receive from him and to understand his speech: {and these parables we strike for people; and none understands them but those who know} (sūrat al-ʿankabūt 29:43).

then we must understand that god, glorified and exalted, laid down moderation in the whole affair, in all dealings — in dealing with oneself, and dealing with god, and dealing with people. god, exalted be he, laid down moderation and balance between excess and negligence, and it is the upright islamic way, which requires of a person in dealing with god, glorified and exalted, that he not take up the whole of his time in worship and so neglect the rights of himself and the rights of people. for this is not approved in the revealed law and god does not approve it for his servants; and he has never charged human beings with being angels. rather human beings eat and drink and grow weary and sleep and fall ill — and the revealed law has attached rulings to these contingencies that befall them.

for that reason the prophet, god bless him and grant him peace, said: "when the servant falls ill or travels, god says to his angels: look at what my servant used to do in his health and his residence, and write it down for him." this entails that god, glorified and exalted, lightened the burden for the traveller and the sick, and informed his angels of that.

therefore a person must know that these contingencies that befall him and the states that come upon him have an effect upon him in himself; and from here he cannot take up the whole of his time in the aspect of devotion — just as he cannot take up the whole of his time in the affairs of this world and neglect the concerns of the hereafter, for that is the condition of the worshippers of this world and its people, whose life is like the life of beasts and cattle: {and those who disbelieve take their enjoyment and eat as the cattle eat, and the fire is their lodging} (sūrat muḥammad 47:12).

so if a person knows that he has two abodes — the abode of the hereafter and the abode of this world — he prefers the hereafter to this world and gives precedence to its rights; but even so he does not neglect his share of this world, and knows that he has been charged with an obligation about which he was not consulted and whose opinion was not taken, and that the one who charged him is the knowing, the aware, and has laid down for him the rulings relating to this world and the rulings relating to the hereafter. he must be moderate in seeking them both together, and his life must be ordered upon this basis.

the time of the prayer — the most important address directed to a person in it is this address to perform the prescribed, obligatory prayer; and nothing can conflict with it except the necessities which a person needs with a necessitous need. anything other than that cannot be given precedence over the prayer. for this reason umar, may god be pleased with him, wrote to his governors: "the most important of your affairs in my view is the prayer. whoever preserves it and keeps it up has preserved his religion; and whoever wastes it will be even more wasteful of what is other than it."

likewise a person must realise that the affairs of the hereafter are also not upon a single degree in the address. among them are the obligatory duties (farāʾiḍ), and among them are the sunnah acts, and among them are the recommended acts (mandūbāt). and the obligatory duties are of two kinds: individually obligatory (farḍ ʿayn) and communally obligatory (farḍ kifāyah). and the individually obligatory ones are of two kinds: those with a constricted time and those with an ample time.

so let a person begin with the individually obligatory duty with a constricted time, for it takes precedence over others; then after it with the individually obligatory duty with an ample time; then with the communally obligatory duty; and so on. so he orders these rulings with understanding and according to their ranks which the lawgiver placed them in.

a person cannot begin with the sunnah act before the obligatory (wājib): if obligatory duties are upon him whose time has come, how should he occupy himself with what is below them of the sunnah acts and the recommended acts? and if he has obligatory duties with a constricted time and obligatory duties whose time is ample, he must begin with the one whose time the lawgiver has constricted, because the constriction of its time entails hastening to it and not postponing or delaying it.

likewise in the affairs of this world, a person must realise that his dealings in this worldly life — even in the rights of his own self, in his dealing with himself — are of many varied kinds. among them are rights that pertain to the spirit and to spiritual matters, and among these are his repentance and his turning to god, glorified and exalted, and his sincerity in his work; these are among the rights of his own self. if he falls short in it and neglects it, one aspect of his composition will remain paralysed, unable to move, and the rest of his body cannot bear it up. for the person whose spirit perceives nothing of the taste of worship and does not savour it and does not savour the sweetness of faith is paralysed — one of his aspects is crippled.

and the person who goes to excess in spiritual matters at the expense of bodily ones — his time is paralysed by thinking, and yet at the same time he is neglectful of the work of the limbs also; he will be obsessive, filled with insinuating doubts and suppositions, and unable to perform his obligatory duties and his binding duties.

likewise the rights of the body are of varied kinds: the body has a right to nourishment, and a right to sleep, and a right to rest, and a right to covering, and so on. the benefits of the human being — their four foundations are those which god undertook for adam in the garden, saying: {truly it is yours that you shall not be hungry in it nor naked, and that you shall not thirst in it nor be exposed to the sun's heat} (sūrat ṭā hā 20:118–119). and the meaning of "be exposed to the sun's heat" is to be out in the sun — that is, shelter. so food and drink and clothing and shelter: these are the foundations of the benefits which are the rights of a person's body in respect of his own self; and there must be balance among them.

how, for example, should a person wear the finest clothes while he is hungry? is he a man of reason, to buy the finest clothes and die of hunger? this is not upright; rather it is without balance and without moderation. and likewise the case if he goes to extremes in kinds of foods while he wears rags and tatters of clothing — is this moderate either? by no means; this is not upright guidance. therefore a person must observe the balance among the rights of his own self.

and so on: if a person takes the bulk of his time for sleep and rest and leaves the little of it and the slight margin for work, is he moderate and balanced? by no means — because he has diverted to sleep more than its share.

god's blessings ought to be looked at with a view to moderation, on the model of budgets. you know budgets: this ministry, its budget is such-and-such, and it is divided into headings — such-and-such a heading for housing, and such-and-such a heading for employees' salaries, and such-and-such a heading for operations, and such-and-such a heading for the maintenance of installations. these headings cannot encroach upon one another, nor can disorder occur among them. and if inequality occurs among them, it arises from inequality in the charges likewise — so it is justice and not wrong at that point.

and so with his dealing with his family: a person must be moderate in his dealing with his family. whoever has two parents — how should he be, for example, dutiful to his father and undutiful to his mother, or dutiful to his mother and undutiful to his father? this is not balanced nor moderate and cannot be accepted in any way whatever. rather he must render to each holder of a right his right. so he begins with the right of the mother in a case of constraint: if he finds only the right of one of them, he begins with the right of the mother, because the prophet, god bless him and grant him peace, began with her. but in a case of amplitude he must observe the rights of both together and be dutiful to both together. god has joined their rights in his book in a number of verses, such as his words, exalted be he: {and worship god and associate nothing with him, and to parents excellence} (sūrat al-nisāʾ 4:36); and his words, exalted be he: {and your lord has decreed that you worship none but him, and to parents excellence} (sūrat al-isrāʾ 17:23); and his words, exalted be he: {and we have enjoined upon the human being excellence towards his parents} (sūrat al-aḥqāf 46:15).

all of this requires balance in observing the rights of both together. and likewise the children: their rights must be observed with equality. it is established as sound in the report of al-nu'man ibn bashir, may god be pleased with them both, in the ṣaḥīḥ, that his father bashir ibn sad gave him a garden in medina, and amrah bint rawahah, who is the mother of al-nu'man, insisted that he have the messenger of god, god bless him and grant him peace, witness that. he said: so he took me to the messenger of god, god bless him and grant him peace, and said: "messenger of god, bear witness that i have given this son of mine, al-nu'man, my garden." he said: "have you given the like of it to all your children?" he said: "no." he said: "have someone other than me bear witness to this, for i do not bear witness to injustice. be conscious of god and treat your children equally." and in another transmission: "and be just between your children."

so here there must be justice between the children in gifts, and in upbringing, and in undertaking all their interests — counsel and guidance and the rest of their many rights, of which many people neglect what relates to counsel and teaching and upbringing. many people, when they hear of rights, turn their minds only to material rights, so they suppose that children's rights are maintenance and housing, and neglect what is other than that of their rights — upbringing and supplication and counsel and teaching and other matters which are more emphatic and greater than their rights to maintenance and housing.

then the prophet, god bless him and grant him peace, when he here rejected bashir ibn sad's lack of justice between his children, did not say that all cases would be thus. rather there is no doubt that differentiation may also occur between children: whoever among them bears charges — he has a household and children and he is poor — there is no doubt that his father may single him out with what he does not single out another with, one who does not bear that burden. and whoever is more excellent and more dutiful — there is no doubt that he deserves a greater reward than the one below him deserves.

for that reason it is established as sound from aisha, may god be pleased with her, that abu bakr, may god be pleased with him, said to her in his final illness: "i had given you the harvest of fifty wasqs from my palm-grove at al-aliyah. had you taken it, you would have owned it; but as for today, it is the property of an heir."

so abu bakr al-siddiq, may god be pleased with him, singled out aisha, may god be pleased with her, with what god had distinguished her by of excellence and dutifulness and other things — for she is decidedly the most excellent of his children. so he distinguished her and singled her out with this gift, the harvest of fifty wasqs from his palm-grove at al-aliyah; but he taught her the ruling at his death. he said: "had you taken it" — that is, taken possession of it — "you would have owned it. but as for today," after he had reached the point of the death-agony and of dying, "it is the property of an heir" — that is, there is no bequest to an heir. for aisha had not taken possession of it, so it became in the position of a bequest; and the gift of a sick person is in the position of a bequest; and there is no bequest to an heir. for that reason he said: "had you taken it you would have owned it; but as for today it is the property of an heir."

so this kind of thing does not contradict this moderation among the children in observing their rights.

and likewise we must know that when the lawgiver distinguished the male children over the daughters in inheritance, that does not mean wronging the daughters in their rights. it is obligatory upon the parents to observe the rights of the daughters just as they observe the rights of the sons, with no difference: what is upon them of maintenance and housing and upbringing and supplication and counsel and teaching — in these rights the males and the females among their children are equal.

god, exalted be he, singled out the males in inheritance with the doubling only on the basis of other matters, among them the charges he laid upon them; for the honouring is according to the measure of the charge. for god, exalted be he, placed upon the male children the blood-money and did not place that upon the daughters; and placed upon the men the bridal gifts and placed nothing of that upon the women; and placed upon the men the maintenance payments and placed nothing of that upon the women. for the woman — the maintenance of her husband is not obligatory upon her even if she is rich and he is poor; and the maintenance of her brother is not obligatory upon her even if he is poor and she is rich; and the maintenance of her child is not obligatory upon her even if she is rich and he is poor. these are matters by which god distinguished the men in respect of charges; and correspondingly he increased their share in inheritance — and this is of the justice of god, glorified and exalted.

but even so, in bequest and in endowment and in other things he made them equal; and the siblings through the mother are likewise equal, their male and their female, in inheritance. all of this requires moderation and balance in dealing.

likewise dealing with neighbours: a person must realise that his doing good to some of them does not justify his doing ill to others, and that it is upon him to do good to all, and that his good should extend beyond himself. and he must know that the neighbour has a great right, which the messenger of god, god bless him and grant him peace, urged, saying: "gabriel did not cease urging me concerning the neighbour, until i thought he would give him a share of inheritance."

and even so, the nearest of the neighbours in door to the house is the most entitled to the bond, as the prophet, god bless him and grant him peace, said: "the neighbour has the better right by his nearness" — and in a transmission in the ṣaḥīḥ of al-bukhari: "the neighbour has the better right by his proximity"; and ṣaqab and saqab mean nearness. what is meant by that is that whoever is nearer has the better right to the rights of a neighbour.

and when abu dharr asked the messenger of god, god bless him and grant him peace, about the rights of neighbours — with which of them does one begin? — he said: "the nearest of them in house" — that is, the nearest of them in dwelling to you; so you begin with this one before others, because the relation of neighbourhood arises from nearness of place. so whoever has the better claim to this relation, which is the basis of the right that follows in the revealed law, takes precedence over another.

then the rights of the neighbour also are of two kinds: some relate to the negative side, that is, to refraining from harm; and some relate to doing good. and the negative side always takes precedence over the positive side in the charges, as the prophet, god bless him and grant him peace, said: "what i have forbidden you, avoid it; and what i have commanded you, do of it what you are able."

so refraining from harm takes precedence over doing good. for if a person does good and gives charity to the poor but in return for that reproaches them and harms them, what is the benefit of his charity and his bond? for he nullifies it by the reproach and the harm; and this is what god forbade in his book, and he made clear that a mere kindly word is better than a charity followed by harm, saying: {a kindly word and forgiveness are better than a charity followed by harm} (sūrat al-baqarah 2:263).

likewise, in looking at others generally there must be this moderation and balance. a person bears witness over people with the witness of the community, because he is one of the individuals of the community of muhammad, god bless him and grant him peace; and this community are god's witnesses over people, a function god assigned it in his book, saying: {and thus we made you a middle community, that you may be witnesses over people and that the messenger may be a witness over you} (sūrat al-baqarah 2:143).

but this witness is only a witness in the aggregate, not over individuals. therefore it is not upon a person to reckon himself a warden over others, watching their movements and their stillnesses, tracking their slips and their faults — this is not part of a person's charge. it is upon him to act according to what is outwardly apparent and according to what he sees. so whoever he sees to be of the people of good outwardly, he thinks well of him inwardly and commits his inner state to god, exalted be he, and deals with him according to what appears from him.

the person whom you know only in the mosque, who when the caller to prayer calls is among the first of the foremost to the first row, and you do not know what he does in his house — it is not for you to think anything of him but good, because you know nothing in him but good. and the person whom you have never known except in the houses of god, in the mosques — there is no doubt that you bear witness for him to faith, as has come in the report of al-tirmidhi that the messenger of god, god bless him and grant him peace, said: "when you see a man frequenting the mosques, bear witness for him to faith" — because god, exalted be he, says: {only he shall maintain the mosques of god who believes in god} (sūrat al-tawbah 9:18).

from here, it is not upon you to track people's faults nor to uncover them. god, glorified and exalted, has forbidden spying and prying, and said in sūrat al-ḥujurāt: {and do not spy} (sūrat al-ḥujurāt 49:12). and the prophet, god bless him and grant him peace, said: "do not spy and do not pry." and he made clear that whoever spies upon people and seeks to see what they have concealed of their circumstances must inevitably be exposed by god in this world and the hereafter. it is established as sound from the prophet, god bless him and grant him peace, that he said: "whoever conceals a muslim, god will conceal him in this world and the hereafter." and in the other report: "whoever tracks the fault of a muslim in order to disgrace him, god will track his fault; and whoever's fault god tracks, he will disgrace him."

therefore the muslim must realise that among the rights of the muslims upon him is that he deal with them according to what appears from them and according to what is outwardly seen, and that he commit their inner states to god, glorified and exalted.

this is not restricted to those he associates and lives with; rather it includes the predecessors of the community and those of it who have died. those of this community who have died — if you hear in their biographies nothing but good and righteousness, and hear nothing but praise of them by right, then you cannot track their slips and their faults and search them out. "that was a community that has passed away: theirs is what they earned and yours is what you have earned, and you will not be asked about what they used to do."

and likewise what occurred between them and what arose among them of disagreements, even if that be in the well-known transmitted history of the community, as occurred between the companions of muhammad, god bless him and grant him peace, and god be pleased with them all — it is upon you to be balanced and moderate in it, and not to show enmity to any of them, and to hold allegiance to them all by virtue of their allegiance to god and to his messenger, god bless him and grant him peace; and to know that they are the most entitled of people to the intercession of the prophet, god bless him and grant him peace. for their precedence in islam and their companionship of the messenger of god, god bless him and grant him peace, and their striving alongside him — all of that entails the effacing of their slips.

god, glorified and exalted, made clear his excusing of many of them for certain errors they fell into, and said, exalted be he, concerning the day of uhud, in assessing that great campaign: {truly those of you who turned away on the day the two hosts met — satan only made them slip because of some of what they had earned; and god has indeed pardoned them} (sūrat āl ʿimrān 3:155). "and god has indeed pardoned them" — this sentence is decisive over what they fell short in and what occurred from them; for god's pardon, glorified and exalted, is decisive over all of that and does away with it.

and especially those with whom god was pleased with his greatest good pleasure, after which there is no anger, such as those who were present at badr and those who pledged allegiance beneath the tree: upon those there came down god's greatest good pleasure, after which there is no anger, so their sins do not occur except forgiven, because the good pleasure preceded the sin. so what occurs from them afterwards, after the death of the prophet, god bless him and grant him peace — even if it were of wars and the killing of the soul which god has forbidden, without right — god's greatest good pleasure, after which there is no anger, preceded that; so their sins do not occur except forgiven.

it is established as sound from the prophet, god bless him and grant him peace, that he said: "by him in whose hand is the soul of muhammad, no one who pledged allegiance beneath the tree will enter the fire." and it is established as sound from him in the ṣaḥīḥ of muslim that he said, when they had finished the pledge: "you are the best of the people of the earth." and god made clear his good pleasure with them in his words: {god was indeed pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you beneath the tree, and he knew what was in their hearts, so he sent down tranquillity upon them and rewarded them with a near victory} (sūrat al-fatḥ 48:18).

so those upon whom god's good pleasure came down — how should people's tongues reach them afterwards? for nothing can occur from them except what is pleasing in the sight of god, even if it were a forbidden sin which forgiveness preceded.

likewise those who followed them in excellence, the successors to them in excellence in the various ages — there is no doubt that they are human beings who err and are right. and in the ṣaḥīḥ of muslim the prophet, god bless him and grant him peace, said: "by him in whose hand is the soul of muhammad, if you did not err and then repent, god would take you away and bring a people who err and repent and he forgives them."

so we know that human beings have errors; but those errors will be weighed on the day of resurrection, and against them their good deeds. whoever's scale of good deeds outweighs his scale of evil deeds will certainly be among the people of the garden; for the outweighing of the scale of good deeds on the day of resurrection is decisive over what was in the other scale.

if a person realises that and knows it, the matter becomes light upon him — and especially when he compares it with himself. if you read in the biographies of one of those who have passed, or it is related to you of one of those who went before among the people of knowledge or the people of righteousness whom you did not live to see, some errors which you know to be errors and whose contrary evidence you know — look at what you yourself fall into of error while you know it to be an error and know the evidence against it. if you know that, you will deal justly with others. for the prophet, god bless him and grant him peace, said: "all the sons of adam are much given to error, and the best of those who err are the ones who repent."

and by your watching over your own errors, your inclination to look at the errors of others is lessened. malik reported in the muwatta, and ahmad in al-zuhd, from yahya ibn said, that it reached him that jesus son of mary used to say: "do not speak much in other than the remembrance of god, or your hearts will harden; for the hard heart is far from god, but you do not know. and do not look at the sins of people as though you were lords; and look at your own sins as though you were servants. for people are of two kinds: one afflicted and one spared. so have mercy upon the people of affliction, and praise god for well-being."

if you come upon some of the slips of others, know that god, glorified and exalted, concealed you when he did not let others come upon your own faults, which you know and cannot deny. so let it be a spur for you towards obedience to god and perfecting his worship and repenting to him of your slips and asking forgiveness much.

and it is also among the rights of those who went before that you ask forgiveness for them if you come upon their errors. for god, exalted be he, says: {and those who came after them say: our lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith, and do not place in our hearts rancour towards those who believe. our lord, you are kind, merciful} (sūrat al-ḥashr 59:10).

the imam malik, may god have mercy on him, heard a man of the khawarij reviling some of the companions of the messenger of god, god bless him and grant him peace, so he called him and said: "are you of the first foremost among the emigrants?" he said: "no." he said: "then are you of the helpers who gave shelter and support?" he said: "no." he said: "then i bear witness that you are not of those who followed them in excellence" — for those who followed them in excellence, god described their state as saying: {our lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith, and do not place in our hearts rancour towards those who believe. our lord, you are kind, merciful}.

then, in this chapter, it is upon a person to look at whoever is above him in obedience and to look at whoever is below him in the affairs of this world, as the prophet, god bless him and grant him peace, made clear, saying: "look, in the affairs of the hereafter, to whoever is above you; and look, in the affairs of this world, to whoever is below you" — for that is more fitting that you should not belittle god's blessing upon you.

so it is upon a person to look at whoever is above him in the affairs of religion. whoever prays more than he, and remembers god more, and recites the qur'an more, and keeps more constantly to ritual purity and to the mosques, and restrains his limbs more from disobedience — this one is a model and an example who ought to be followed, even if he himself is more learned than that one, and even if he is higher than him in lineage, and even if he has more understanding than him. for the benefit of all of that is only what brings one near to god; and none of these matters counts for anything except what comes into the scale of good deeds from it.

all a person's deeds on the day of resurrection go to the balance; and the balance has two pans and a pointer, and god does not wrong people in anything. so whoever's scale of good deeds outweighs his scale of evil deeds, his recompense is the garden; and whoever's scale of evil deeds outweighs, he will be driven to the fire — we ask god for safety and well-being.

by that you must be moderate in your view of others, and especially if you know that they have excellence and great good deeds; then correspondingly your view of their evil deeds must not be decisive over your view of their good deeds. for if you look only with the eye of displeasure and never look with the eye of moderation and balance, you will see only with that eye and will see nothing but what is detested and hateful. and if you always look with the eye of approval, you will see nothing but what is pleasing.

and the eye of approval is required to be used in certain cases, such as looking at the companions and the successors and their followers — the generations which the prophet, god bless him and grant him peace, bore witness to with commendation: the best of generations is the generation among whom i was sent, then those who follow them, then those who follow them. and in his words, god bless him and grant him peace: "a company of people will go raiding, and it will be said: is there among you anyone who saw muhammad? and they will say: yes — and victory will be granted to them. then a company of people will go raiding, and it will be said: is there among you anyone who saw one who saw muhammad? and they will say: yes — and victory will be granted to them. then a company of people will go raiding, and it will be said: is there among you anyone who saw one who saw one who saw muhammad? and they will say: yes — and victory will be granted to them."

so those people whom god distinguished and preferred are looked at with the eye of approval always, and their slips are not sought out, and nothing is supposed of them but the best of constructions, and evil is never supposed of them.

and those below them among people — if you wish to appraise them you must look at them with the eye of due consideration; if you do not look with the eye of approval, then do not look with the eye of displeasure. for the eye of displeasure will display to you all the faults, so that you suppose this person to be a devil, because you will overlook everything in him of aspects of good.

this is what caused the feet of the khawarij to slip in their appraisal of the companions of muhammad, god bless him and grant him peace. uthman ibn affan, may god be pleased with him — and he was the successor of the messenger of god, god bless him and grant him peace, and the leader of the muslims, and they were wronging him, and they besieged him and killed him in the sacred month in the sacred land, wronged, may god be pleased with him — he was asked, when they had withheld water from him while he was in the house, and it was said: "why do they treat you with this treatment?" and he said: "falsehood has shown me to them as a devil" — meaning: falsehood has made me a devil in their eyes.

for they did not look at his precedence in islam, nor at his rights, nor at his trials in islam, nor at the testimony of the messenger of god, god bless him and grant him peace, for him by name to the garden, nor at the fact that god's greatest good pleasure, after which there is no anger, had come down upon him, so that all his sins are forgiven and forgiveness preceded them. they looked at none of this; rather they began to look at him as a human being like themselves — indeed they supposed him worse than themselves — and appraised him only by some deeds which they saw, and left what stood against them of the immense, great deeds which they neglected. this is what error in the appraisal of people arises from.

then, supposing that you did look at some faults for a purpose recognised in the revealed law, such as the appraisal of the transmitters of hadith, for example, and of the bearers of knowledge — you must also be a man of scrupulousness and a man of restraint of tongue, and must not exceed the measure that the evidence establishes and the proof establishes.
