t: The Character of the Muslim
a: شخصية المسلم
b:
*[site synopsis]* the change sought today in our islamic world has as its basis the changing of the souls of the muslims for the better, and that is not accomplished except by rebuilding character, by forming it and by purifying it (tazkiyah) through this mighty religion. for the serious and the sincere, the work of building the self knows neither stopping nor stumbling; with them it continues until death comes to them. the features of the muslim's character do not become clear except through great and continuous effort, and through a building of the self that is sound and complete and rests on foundations to which the revealed law has called and which it has set out.

## the muslim's character is what distinguishes him from everyone else

in the name of god, the all-merciful, the mercy-giving. praise belongs to god, lord of the worlds. i ask god's blessing and peace upon the one sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his companions, and upon all who have taken guidance from his guidance and followed his practice until the day of judgement. peace be upon you, and god's mercy and his blessings. to proceed: every creed and every sect, and every ideology, has values and foundations that make it clear and that distinguish it from everything else. this religion — which is the true religion with god, glorified and exalted is he — has distinguishing marks: it is by them that it is distinguished from everything else; it is by them that the level of faith rises in the hearts of those who hold it; and it is by them that a person makes his faith excellent, so that he becomes excellent in his islam. without them — even were he a believer with his heart, his tongue and some of his limbs — his islam is not excellent. and excellence of islam is what the messenger, god bless him and grant him peace, made the condition for good deeds blotting out bad ones …
r:
إن التغيير المنشود اليوم في عالمنا الإسلامي أساسه تغيير نفوس المسلمين إلى الأحسن، ولا يتم ذلك إلا بإعادة بناء الشخصية وتربيتها وتزكيتها بهذا الدين العظيم، وإن عملية بناء النفس عند الجادين المخلصين لا تعرف التوقف ولا التعثر، بل هي مستمرة عندهم حتى يأتيهم الموت، ولا تتضح معالم شخصية المسلم إلا بجهد عظيم متواصل، وبناء للنفس محكم متكامل يقوم على أسس دعا إليها الشرع وبينها.
شخصية المسلم هي التي تميزه عمن سواه:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين، وأصلي وأسلم على من بعث رحمة للعالمين، وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين. السلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته. أما بعد: فإن كل ملة ونحلة وكل أيديولوجية لها قيم وأسس تبينها وتميزها عما سواها، وإن هذا الدين الذي هو الدين الحق عند الله سبحانه وتعالى له ميزات هي التي تميزه عما سواه، وهي التي يزداد بها منسوب الإيمان في قلوب ذويه، وهي التي يحسن الإنسان بها إيمانه فيصبح حسن الإسلام، وبدونها ولو كان مؤمناً بقلبه ولسانه وبعض جوارحه فإن إسلامه غير حسن، وحسن الإسلام هو الذي شرطه الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم في تكفير الحسنات للسيئات ...

t: Understanding Disagreement Rightly
a: فقه الخلاف
b:
*[site synopsis]* disagreement is one of the things that living together cannot do without. god made human beings differ in constitution, in disposition and in intellect, and this variety and this difference result from the difference of intellects; and those whose intellects differ may well differ in their inclinations, and their views and their positions may not be one. all of that is a fact. understanding disagreement rightly rests on setting out the danger of disagreement and warning against it, on setting out its kinds, its proprieties and its remedy, and on what is permissible in the way of disagreement and what is not.

## disagreement is one of the things living together cannot do without

in the name of god, the all-merciful, the mercy-giving. praise belongs to god, lord of the worlds. i ask god's blessing and peace upon the one sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his companions, and upon all who have taken guidance from his guidance and followed his practice until the day of judgement. the subject of this lesson is "understanding disagreement rightly", and the elements we shall take up in it are:

first: the warning against splitting apart and against disagreement.
second: the kinds of disagreement.
third: the proprieties of those who differ with one another.
fourth: the remedy for disagreement.

disagreement is one of the things living together cannot do without. god made human beings differ in constitution, in disposition and in intellect, and gave some of them distinction over others; and this variety in which god has set them entails that they should not agree on certain questions. their not agreeing on it is an enrichment and a benefit to human beings, and a benefit to the people of the earth ..
r:
إن الخلاف من ضرورات التعايش، فقد جعل الله البشر متفاوتين في الخِلقة والخلق والعقل، وهذا التنوع والاختلاف ناتج عن اختلاف العقول، ومن تفاوتت عقولهم فبالإمكان أن تتفاوت اتجاهاتهم، وألا تتحد رؤاهم ومواقفهم، وكل ذلك واقع، وفقه الخلاف يرتكز على بيان خطر الاختلاف والتحذير منه، وبيان أنواعه، وآدابه، وعلاجه، وما يجوز من الخلاف وما لا يجوز.
الخلاف من ضرورات التعايش:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين، وأصلي وأسلم على من بعث رحمة للعالمين، وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه، واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين. موضوع هذا الدرس: (فقه الخلاف) والعناصر التي سنتعرض لها فيه هي: أولاً: التحذير من الفرقة والاختلاف. ثانيًا: أنوع الخلاف. ثالثًا: آداب المتخالفين. رابعًا: علاج الخلاف. إن الخلاف من ضرورات التعايش، فقد جعل الله البشر متفاوتين في الخِلقة والخلق والعقل، وميَّز بعضهم على بعض، وهذا التنوع الذي جعلهم الله عليه مقتضٍ لئلا يتفقوا في بعض المسائل، وعدم اتفاقهم فيه إثراء وفائدة للبشر، وفائدة لأهل الأرض ..

t: Examples of the Sacrifices of the Shinqiti Scholars
a: نماذج من تضحيات علماء الشناقطة
b:
*[site synopsis]* the scholars are the heirs of the prophets, whom god chooses to carry his religion and to convey it to people. among these scholars who sacrificed much and who strove to spread knowledge and to raise the banner of the religion are the scholars of shinqit — except that they did not become famous among people, and had no great renown in the world, despite the severity of their hardship and their endurance of harsh conditions for the sake of knowledge from the fifth century onward, and indeed before it. in this material the sheikh gives examples that tell of the efforts of the shinqitis and of their sacrifices in preserving knowledge and establishing the religion.

## the scholars are god's chosen and the heirs of the prophets

in the name of god, the all-merciful, the mercy-giving. praise belongs to god, lord of the worlds. i ask god's blessing and peace upon our prophet muhammad, master of the first and the last, and upon his family and his companions, and upon all who have taken guidance from his guidance and followed his practice until the day of judgement. to proceed: god, glorified and exalted is he, established the proof against people by the messengers whom he sent as bearers of good news and as warners, to point people to the road with which their creator, glorified and exalted is he, is pleased. there is no community but that a messenger went before it in it, calling it to what its creator, glorified and exalted is he, is pleased with from it.

and when god sealed the messages of the messengers to the people of the earth, he made the scholars the heirs of the prophets. he made them the bearers of the torch of truth and those who raise its banner, striving in its path and raising high the word of god, glorified and exalted is he, by what they expend and what they sacrifice. god, glorified and exalted is he, made that easy for them and helped them to it, and chose them — a true choosing — from among his creation …
r:
العلماء ورثة الأنبياء، يختارهم الله لحمل دينه وتبليغه للناس، ومن هؤلاء العلماء الذين ضحوا كثيراً وجاهدوا في نشر العلم ورفع علَم الدين علماء الشناقطة، إلا أنهم لم يشتهروا بين الناس، ولم يكن لهم في الدنيا ذكر كثير، بالرغم من شدة عنائهم وتحملهم الظروف القاسية في سبيل العلم منذ القرن الخامس، بل قبله. وقد ذكر الشيخ في هذه المادة نماذج تنبئ عن جهود الشناقطة وتضحياتهم في حفظ العلم وإقامة الدين.
العلماء صفوة الله وورثة الأنبياء:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين، وأصلي وأسلم على نبينا محمد سيد الأولين والآخرين، وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين. أما بعد: فإن الله سبحانه وتعالى أقام الحجة على الناس بالرسل الذين أرسلهم مبشرين ومنذرين ليدلوا الناس على الطريق الذي يرتضي منهم خالقهم سبحانه وتعالى، فما من أمة إلا وفرط فيها رسول دعاها إلى ما يرتضيه منها خالقها سبحانه وتعالى. وعندما ختم الله رسالات الرسل إلى أهل الأرض جعل العلماء ورثة الأنبياء، فجعلهم الحاملين لمشعل الحق والرافعين للوائه، يجاهدون في سبيله ويعلون كلمة الله سبحانه وتعالى بما يبذلون ويضحون، وقد يسرهم الله سبحانه وتعالى لذلك وأعانهم عليه، واختارهم اختياراً من بين خلقه...

t: The Names and Attributes Series [1]
a: سلسلة الأسماء والصفات [1]
b:
*[site synopsis]* sūrat al-ikhlāṣ comprises the affirmation of god's oneness and of his being the one eternally besought (ṣamad); and from it the scholars derived the five negating attributes in respect of god, exalted is he, as the sheikh, may god preserve him, has explained them.

## the division of things in respect of independence of, and need for, a substrate and a determiner

in the name of god, the all-merciful, the mercy-giving. praise belongs to god, lord of the worlds, and god's blessing and peace upon our prophet muhammad and upon his family and his companions all together. our sheikh, may god preserve him, said in his versification on the names and attributes: *[and he, exalted is he, is one, single, eternally besought; whoever has said that he is united with his creation has deviated.]*

as for the word "al-fard", the single, it has come in reports and has not occurred in the qur'an. as for "al-ṣamad", the attribute of ṣamadiyyah is affirmed of him, and it is absolute independence of his creation. absolute independence means being in no need of either a substrate or a determiner.

things, as regards need of and independence of a substrate and a determiner, fall into four divisions. the first kind: what needs both a substrate and a determiner together — and that is the attributes of created things. they need the substrate in which they subsist, because an attribute does not subsist by itself but needs a substrate to be in, as with whiteness and blackness, tallness and shortness: these must have an essence in which they subsist, and they need a determiner. by "the determiner" is meant the creator, who marks off this created thing by six out of twelve …
r:
اشتملت سورة الإخلاص على إثبات وحدانية الله وصمديته، وأخذ منها العلماء الصفات الخمس السلبية في حق الله تعالى كما شرحها الشيخ حفظه الله تعالى.
انقسام الأشياء من حيث الغنى والحاجة إلى المحل والمخصص:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين، وصلى الله وسلم على نبينا محمد وعلى آله وصحبه أجمعين. قال شيخنا حفظه الله في منظومته في الأسماء والصفات: [ وهو تعالى أحد فرد صمد ألحد من قال بخلقه اتحد ] بالنسبة للفظ (الفرد) فقد جاء في أحاديث ولم يرد في القرآن، وأما (الصمد) فإن صفة الصمدية مثبتة له، وهي الغنى المطلق عن خلقه، والغنى المطلق معناه: الاستغناء عن المحل والمخصص جميعاً. والأشياء فيما يتعلق بالحاجة والغنى عن المحل والمخصص أربعة أقسام: النوع الأول: ما يحتاج إلى المحل والمخصص معاً: وهو صفات المخلوقين، فهي محتاجة إلى المحل الذي تقوم به؛ لأنها صفة والصفة لا تقوم بنفسها بل تحتاج إلى محل تكون فيه، وذلك مثل البياض والسواد، والطول والقصر، فهذه لا بد لها من ذات تقوم بها، وتحتاج إلى المخصص. والمخصص المقصود به الخالق الذي يميز هذا المخلوق بست من اثنتي عشرة...

t: The Names and Attributes Series [2]
a: سلسلة الأسماء والصفات [2]
b:
*[site synopsis]* the attributes of affirmation have come set out in detail in the qur'an and the sunnah. as for negation, it has not been set out in detail except in the denial of a consort, a partner, a progenitor and offspring. the way of the early generations in dealing with the attributes of god, exalted is he, was to affirm them and to stop at the texts in which they have come, without likening him to creation and without stripping him of them.

## the denial that god, mighty and majestic, has a consort, a progenitor or offspring

## what is meant by the denial that god has an equal

then he said: {and there is none equal to him}. this is a confirmation of everything that preceded, and it needs no connective in it. you might say: why did he not say "and there is none equal to him"? the answer is that the meaning of "there is none equal to him" is that he has no consort, no offspring and no progenitor — because "al-kufʾ" is the counterpart.

one says "al-kufw" with a wāw, "al-kufʾ" with a hamzah, and "al-kufuʾ" with two ḍammahs; and all of these are read. the reading of nafiʿ, ibn kathir and ibn amir is "kufuʾan" with the hamzah, and the reading of the kufans is "kufwan" with the wāw — except that shuʿbah reads it "kufwan" with the fāʾ vowelless, with sukūn, while others read it with ḍammah.

two things are meant by this. the first is the denial of any likeness whatsoever, because equality requires some measure of shared resemblance. human beings, in respect of their being formed alike, are equals: not one of them exceeds another by a limb, for instance; rather they are one and the same form. it is for this that al-shafi'i, may god have mercy on him, said:

*people, in respect of their being formed alike, are equals; their father is adam and the mother is eve.*

the second — and this is the fundamental thing meant by the denial of an equal — is that no one can be his equal or his counterpart so as to marry with him …
r:
لقد جاءت صفات الإثبات مفصلة في القرآن والسنة، أما النفي فلم يفصل إلا في نفي الصاحبة والشريك والوالد والولد، وقد كان منهج السلف في التعامل مع صفات الله تعالى إثباتها والوقوف عند النصوص الواردة بها من غير تشبيه ولا تعطيل.
نفي وجود الصاحبة والوالد والولد لله عز وجل.
المقصود من نفي وجود الكفء لله:
ثم قال: (ليس لَهُ كُفُواً أَحَدٌ) وهذا تقرير لكل ما سبق، ولا يحتاج إلى العطف فيه، يمكن أن تقول: لماذا لم يقل: (وليس لَهُ كُفُواً أَحَدٌ)؟ والجواب: أن معنى أنه (ليس لَهُ كُفُواً أحد): أنه لا صاحبة له ولا ولد ولا والد؛ لأن الكفء هو النظير، يقال: الكفو بالواو، والكفء بالهمزة، والكفؤ بضمتين، وهذه كلها مقروءة، فقراءة نافع و ابن كثير و ابن عامر (كفؤاً) بالهمزة، وقراءة الكوفيين: (كفواً) بالواو لكن شعبة يقرؤها (كفْواً) بإسكان الفاء بالإسكان وغيره يقرؤها بالضم. والمقصود بهذا أمران: أحدهما: نفي التشبيه مطلقاً؛ لأن الكفاءة مقتضية لقدر من الاشتراك في الشبه، فالبشر من جهة التمثيل أكفاء، لا أحد منهم يزيد على آخر بعضو مثلاً، بل هم صورة واحدة؛ ولهذا قال الشافعي رحمه الله: الناس من جهة التمثيل أكفاء أبوهم آدم والأم حواء والثاني: وهو المقصود الأساس من نفي الكفء: أنه لا يمكن أن يكافئه ولا أن يناظره أحد حتى يتزاوج معه...

t: The Names and Attributes Series [3]
a: سلسلة الأسماء والصفات [3]
b:
*[site synopsis]* the attributes that god has affirmed of himself, or that his messenger, god bless him and grant him peace, has affirmed of him, must be affirmed — but without likening him to creation, without interpretation and without stripping him of them.

## the affirmation of the attributes is conditional upon there being no asking how, no comparison, no distortion and no interpretation

he said: *[without any asking how or comparison; and there is for him no distortion or interpretation.]* ......

## the meaning of distortion

"and no distortion": that is, do not distort these texts — the meaning being, do not shift them away from what they originally signify; rather leave them upon what they signify. distorting a text means putting it somewhere other than its own place, as he, exalted is he, said: {they distort words from their places} (sūrat al-nisāʾ 4:46). its origin is the tilting of the pen — that is, inclining it away from being upright, so that in its writing it lies flat; disabling one of the pen's two nib-edges with respect to the other is distortion. and distorting speech means shifting it, cutting it short and moving it from its place to another place.

so, for example, the words that have come in praise of god concerning the face, the two eyes and the two hands: some people shift them so as to make of them a fault and a deficiency. this is distorting the words from their places. god, mighty and majestic, brought them as praise of himself — so how is it to be shifted and made a deficiency and a fault? this is plain distortion …
r:
الصفات التي أثبتها الله لنفسه أو أثبتها له رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم يجب إثباتها؛ لكن بغير تشبيه ولا تأويل ولا تعطيل.
إثبات الصفات مشروط بعدم التكييف والتمثيل والتحريف والتأويل
قال: [من غير ما تكييف أو تمثيل له ولا تحريف أو تأويل] ......
معنى التحريف:
(ولا تحريف): أي: لا تحرف هذه النصوص، والمعنى: ولا تنقل عن دلالتها الأصلية، بل تترك على دلالتها، وتحريف النص معناه: وضعه في غير موضعه، كما قال تعالى:  يُحَرِّفُونَ الْكَلِمَ عَنْ مَوَاضِعِه  [النساء:46] . وأصله تحريف القلم، أي: الميل به عن أن يكون عمودياً، وأن يكون في كتابته أفقياً، فتعطيل إحدى سني القلم عن الأخرى هو تحريف، وتحريف الكلام معناه: نقله وبتره وتحويله من موضعه إلى موضع آخر، فمثلاً الكلام الذي جاء في الثناء على الله من الوجه والعينين واليدين ينقله بعض الناس إلى أن يجعله عيباً ونقصاً، وهذا تحريف للكلم عن مواضعه، فالله عز وجل أتى به ثناءً على نفسه، فكيف ينقل ويجعل نقصاً وعيباً؟ هذا تحريف واضح...

t: The Names and Attributes Series [4]
a: سلسلة الأسماء والصفات [4]
b:
*[site synopsis]* many scholars of the later ages have taken to applying the phrase "the essence of god" (dhāt allāh) to what stands over against his attributes, glorified and exalted is he. this sense is not known in the speech of the arabs, nor in the technical vocabulary of the revealed law. the word "dhāt" is not annexed to proper names except anomalously; the rule is that it be annexed to what is not a proper name, such as "al-ilāh", so that one says "dhāt al-ilāh" — as it was in use in the age of ignorance and in the first period of islam. those among them who used it meant by it his religion, his revealed way and his path, and not the sense of what stands over against an attribute, in which the later scholars apply it.

## applying the word "al-dhāt" to god, mighty and majestic

our sheikh, may god preserve him, said:

*[one says "his self", as he said, "your lord has prescribed…" — the verse. but whoever ascribes a dhāt to him has meant that which is his: his religion, his revealed way, his path. the rule is that it be annexed to "al-ilāh", not to a pronoun nor to the word "allāh" — as in what khubayb said when he was crucified, and what al-nabighah al-dhubyani, the sharp-tongued, said — because it is the feminine of "dhū", in which annexation to what is not a proper name is obligatory, on the apparent sense of what ibn malik said when he mentioned what "dhū" requires in this respect: "dhū"; "dhāt" is its feminine; "dhawāt" the plural; and the base form runs as the derived form does. yes — it did come annexed to "allāh", in the untruths of the devout, oft-sighing one; and that is an anomaly, and its counterpart is "dhū bakkah", which likewise is to be accounted anomalous.]*

these lines are all on a single topic, the topic of applying "al-dhāt" to god, glorified and exalted is he …
r:
درج كثير من العلماء في العصور المتأخرة على إطلاق كلمة (ذات الله) على ما يقابل صفاته سبحانه وتعالى، وهذا المعنى غير معروف في لسان العرب ولا في المصطلحات الشرعية، ولا تضاف كلمة (ذات) إلى الأعلام إلا شذوذاً، والأصل أن تضاف إلى غير الأعلام كالإله فيقال: (ذات الإله) كما كانت مستعملة في الجاهلية وفي صدر الإسلام، ويقصد بها عند من أطلقها منهم أنها ملته وشرعته وسبيله، لا بمعنى ما يقابل الصفة كما يطلقها المتأخرون.
إطلاق لفظ (الذات) على الله عز وجل:
قال شيخنا حفظه الله: [ يقال نفسه كما قال كتب ربكم الآية أما من نسب ذاتاً له فقد عنى التي له ملته شرعته سبيله والأصل أن تضاف للإله لا للضمير أو للفظ لله كمثل ما قال خبيب إذ صلب وقال النابغة الذبياني، الذرب لأنها تأنيث ذي الملتزمِ فيه الإضافة لغير العلمِ لظاهر قال ابن مالك وقد ذكر ما يلزم (ذو) في ذا الصدد ذو ذات أنثاه ذوات الجمع وجريان الأصل مثل الفرع نعم أتت مضافةً لله في كذبات القانت الأواه وهو شذوذ ونظيره ذو بكة مما وجهه الشذوذ] هذه الأبيات كلها في مبحث واحد، وهو مبحث إطلاق الذات على الله سبحانه وتعالى...

t: The Names and Attributes Series [5]
a: سلسلة الأسماء والصفات [5]
b:
*[site synopsis]* god, exalted is he, has attributes mentioned in the book and the sunnah. the anthropomorphists (al-mushabbihah) and those who divest god of his attributes (al-muʿaṭṭilah) have dissented over affirming them, and the people of the sunnah have set out rules that answer both groups and that show the sound way of affirming god's essential and active attributes without deviation.

## on the rule that what is said of god's attributes is what is said of his essence and his self

the sheikh, may god preserve him, says:

*[and what we say concerning the attributes of his holiness is derivative of what we say concerning his self ……]*

## answering the anthropomorphists and those who divest god of his attributes by means of this rule

this begins the laying down of rules for the oneness of the names and attributes. the most important of these rules are two. the first is that what is said of the attributes is what is said of the essence, and this is the rule he set in verse in this line, in his words: "and what we say concerning the attributes of his holiness is derivative of what we say concerning his self." that is to say: speech about his attributes is like speech about his essence. this removes every difficulty, whether it comes from the side of those who divest god of his attributes or from the side of the anthropomorphists.

as for the side of those who divest him of his attributes: they do affirm that he has a self, which in their view is the essence; and they know that the created thing has an essence too; and even so, in their view, affirming that he has an essence and that the created thing has an essence does not entail likening him to creation — definitively not, on their own account. what, then, is the difference between the essence and the face, the two hands, the eye, the foot and the shin?!…
r:
لله تعالى صفات مذكورة في الكتاب والسنة، وقد خالف في إثباتها المشبهة والمعطلة، وقد ذكر أهل السنة قواعد ترد على الفرقتين، وتبين الطريقة السليمة في إثبات صفات الله الذاتية والفعلية من غير انحراف.
الكلام على قاعدة (القول في صفات الله كالقول في ذاته ونفسه)
يقول الشيخ حفظه الله: [وما نقول في صفات قدسه فرع الذي نقوله في نفس....]
الرد بالقاعدة على المشبهة والمعطلة:
هذا شروع في وضع قواعد لتوحيد الأسماء والصفات، وهذه القواعد أهمها قاعدتان: أولاهما: أن القول في الصفات كالقول في الذات، وهذه القاعدة هي التي نظمها في هذا البيت بقوله: (وما نقول في صفات قدسه فرع الذي نقوله في نفسه) أي: إن الكلام في صفاته مثل الكلام في ذاته، وهذه مزيلة لكل إشكال، سواء كان من جهة المعطلة أو من جهة المشبهة: أما من جهة المعطلة: فإنهم يثبتون له نفساً هي الذات عندهم، وهم يعرفون أن للمخلوق ذاتاً ومع ذلك لا يقتضي إثبات أن له ذاتاً وأن للمخلوق ذاتاً التشبيه قطعاً عندهم! فما الفرق بينها وبين الوجه واليدين والعين والقدم والساق؟!...

t: The Names and Attributes Series [6]
a: سلسلة الأسماء والصفات [6]
b:
*[site synopsis]* among the active attributes established for god, exalted is he, there are some from which a name of god, exalted is he, is derived, and some that are not so. god has affirmed for himself in his book, and his messenger has affirmed for him, a great many attributes; the sheikh mentions some of them here and explains them.

## some of god's active attributes

the sheikh said:

*[he hears, he sees, he loves, he wonders, he laughs, he is pleased, he answers, he is angry.]*

this whole line contains eight of the active attributes of god, glorified and exalted is he. some of these attributes also require certain of his names. for example: ……

## affirming the attribute of hearing for god, mighty and majestic

his words "he hears": this is an affirmation of the attribute of hearing for god, glorified and exalted is he. god, exalted is he, says: {god has indeed heard the words of her who disputes with you concerning her husband and complains to god, and god hears the two of you conversing} (sūrat al-mujādalah 58:1). this is an affirmation of this active attribute, and it is an affirmation also of the name "the all-hearing" (al-samīʿ), which is a name derived from this attribute.

as for the hearing of god, glorified and exalted is he, the stronger position is that it is of sounds — that is, that it attaches to sounds and does not attach to entities. the theologians of kalām dissented on this, for they say: his hearing attaches to entities and to sounds, and his sight attaches to entities and to visible things. and they have no evidence whatever for this…
r:
الصفات الفعلية الثابتة لله تعالى منها ما اشتق منه اسم الله تعالى، ومنها ما ليست كذلك، وقد أثبت الله لنفسه في كتابه وأثبت له رسوله صفات كثيرة، وقد ذكر الشيخ هنا بعضها وشرحها.
بعض صفات الله الفعلية:
قال الشيخ: [يسمع يبصر يحب يعجب يضحك يرضى يستجيب يغضب] هذا البيت كله يتضمن ثماني صفات من صفات الله سبحانه وتعالى الفعلية، بعض هذه الصفات مقتضية أيضاً لبعض الأسماء من أسمائه، فمثلاً: ......
إثبات صفة السمع لله عز وجل:
قوله: (يسمع): هذا إثبات لصفة السمع لله سبحانه وتعالى، والله تعالى يقول: قَدْ سَمِعَ اللَّهُ قَوْلَ الَّتِي تُجَادِلُكَ فِي زَوْجِهَا وَتَشْتَكِي إِلَى اللَّهِ وَاللَّهُ يَسْمَعُ تَحَاوُرَكُمَا [المجادلة:1] فهذا إثبات لهذه الصفة الفعلية، وهو إثبات أيضاً لاسم (السميع) فهو اسم مشتق من هذه الصفة. وسمع الله سبحانه وتعالى الراجح أنه للأصوات أي: يتعلق بالأصوات، وأنه لا يتعلق بالذوات، وخالف في هذا المتكلمون، فإنهم يقولون: سمعه يتعلق بالذوات والأصوات، وبصره يتعلق بالذوات والمبصرات، وليس لهم على هذا أي دليل...

t: The Names and Attributes Series [7]
a: سلسلة الأسماء والصفات [7]
b:
*[site synopsis]* before us are a number of paired active attributes, all of them indicating the greatness of god, glorified and exalted is he.

## some of god's active attributes

the sheikh, may god preserve him, says:

*[he lowers, he raises; he honours and he abases; he dislikes, he detests; and he guides and he leads astray.]*

we are still in the mention of some of the attributes that come with detailed affirmation in the book of god and in the sunnah of his messenger, may god bless him and grant him peace. among them: ……

## affirming the attributes of lowering and raising for god, mighty and majestic

"lowering and raising": god, glorified and exalted is he, lowers with a lowering that is perceptible and a lowering that is not. perceptible lowering is such as his lowering of the hypocrites in the fire, where he has placed them beneath the disbelievers in it; and such as his lowering of some created things below others. this is perceptible lowering, and of it is the swallowing up of the earth and the like.

as for lowering that is not perceptible, it is such as his lowering of the standing of the disbelievers in this world and in the hereafter — as his lowering, in this world, of the standing of most of the disbelievers below the followers of jesus son of mary. for he has placed his followers above the disbelievers until the day of resurrection, and so lowered the disbelievers beneath the leadership of the followers of jesus until the day of resurrection, as he undertook to jesus in his words: {and placing those who follow you above those who disbelieve until the day of resurrection} (sūrat āl ʿimrān 3:55)…
r:
بين أيدينا عدد من الصفات الفعلية المتقابلة، وكلها مما يدل على عظمة الله سبحانه وتعالى.
من صفات الله الفعلية:
يقول الشيخ حفظه الله: [يخفض يرفع يعز ويـذل يكره يمقت ويهدي ويضل] ما زلنا في ذكر بعض الصفات التي جاءت بالإثبات التفصيلي في كتاب الله وفي سنة رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم، فمنها: ......
إثبات صفة الخفض والرفع لله عز وجل:
(الخفض والرفع): فالله سبحانه وتعالى يخفض خفضاً حسياً وخفضاً معنوياً, فالخفض الحسي مثل خفض المنافقين في النار, حيث جعلهم تحت الكافرين فيها، ومثل خفضه لبعض المخلوقات عن بعض, فهذا هو الخفض الحسي، ومنه الخسف وغيره. وأما الخفض المعنوي: فهو مثل خفضه لمنزلة الكافرين في الدنيا وفي الآخرة، كخفضه في الدنيا لمنزلة أكثر الكافرين على أتباع عيسى بن مريم، فقد جعل أتباعه فوق الكافرين إلى يوم القيامة, فخفض الكافرين تحت رئاسة أتباع عيسى إلى يوم القيامة, كما تعهد بذلك لعيسى في قوله: وَجَاعِلُ الَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوكَ فَوْقَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ [آل عمران:55]...

t: The Names and Attributes Series [8]
a: سلسلة الأسماء والصفات [8]
b:
*[site synopsis]* god, glorified and exalted is he, is described by every perfection and is free of every deficiency. for this reason it belongs to the creed of the people of the sunnah and the community that they affirm for god, mighty and majestic, what he has affirmed for himself or what his messenger, may god bless him and grant him peace, has affirmed for him, and that they deny of him, glorified is he, what he has denied of himself or what his messenger, may god bless him and grant him peace, has denied of him. of this is the affirmation of the attribute of judging, and of his putting questions to his creation while he knows them best, and that he has no equal and no peer, and that nothing can thwart him, glorified and exalted is he.

## affirming the attribute of judgement for god, mighty and majestic

the sheikh, may god preserve him, says: *he judges by the truth; he asks, and he knows best.*

likewise, among the attributes affirmed for god, glorified and exalted is he, is the attribute of judgement (ḥukm). he has affirmed it for himself in many verses, and its affirmation in the qur'an comes in the form of a verb, and comes in the form of a noun with exclusivity.

the noun form is as in the words of god, exalted is he, on the tongue of jacob and joseph, peace be upon them both: {judgement belongs to none but god} (sūrat yūsuf 12:67). jacob, peace be upon him, says: {judgement belongs to none but god; in him i have placed my trust, and in him let all who trust place their trust} (sūrat yūsuf 12:67). and joseph, peace be upon him, says: {judgement belongs to none but god. he has commanded that you worship none but him} (sūrat yūsuf 12:40). and likewise the words of god, exalted is he: {and in whatever you differ, its judgement rests with god} (sūrat al-shūrā 42:10)….
r:
الله سبحانه وتعالى موصوف بكل كمال منزه عن كل نقص، ولهذا فإن من عقيدة أهل السنة والجماعة أنهم يثبتون لله عز وجل ما أثبته لنفسه أو أثبته له رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم، وينفون عنه سبحانه ما نفاه عن نفسه أو نفاه عنه رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم، ومن ذلك إثبات صفة الحكم والاستفهام لخلقه وهو أعلم بهم، وأنه لا ند له ولا نظير ولا يعجزه شيء سبحانه وتعالى.
إثبات صفة الحكم لله عز وجل:
يقول الشيخ حفظه الله: يحكم بالحق يستفهم وهو أعلم. كذلك من الصفات المثبتة لله سبحانه وتعالى صفة الحكم، فقد أثبتها لنفسه في كثير من الآيات، وإثباتها في القرآن جاء بصيغة الفعل، وجاء بصيغة الاسم بالحصر: فصيغة الاسم مثل قول الله تعالى على لسان يعقوب ويوسف عليهما السلام: إِنِ الْحُكْمُ إِلَّا لِلَّهِ [يوسف:67] ، فيعقوب عليه السلام يقول: إِنِ الْحُكْمُ إِلَّا لِلَّهِ عَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ وَعَلَيْهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ الْمُتَوَكِّلُونَ [يوسف:67] ، ويوسف عليه السلام يقول: إِنِ الْحُكْمُ إِلَّا لِلَّهِ أَمَرَ أَلَّا تَعْبُدُوا إِلَّا إِيَّاهُ [يوسف:40] ، وكذلك قول الله تعالى: وَمَا اخْتَلَفْتُمْ فِيهِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ فَحُكْمُهُ إِلَى اللَّهِ [الشورى:10]....

t: The Names and Attributes Series [9]
a: سلسلة الأسماء والصفات [9]
b:
*[site synopsis]* speech is an attribute of perfection for god, glorified and exalted is he. god, exalted is he, has spoken legislative words and cosmic words; and just as he, exalted is he, speaks, so he is also described by silence — but a silence that proceeds from knowledge, so that it too is an attribute of perfection for god, exalted is he.

## god's legislative and cosmic words

the sheikh, may god preserve him, says:

*[and he speaks when he wills, with what he wills …………………]*

speaking is an attribute of perfection for god, mighty and majestic, and his speech, exalted is he, is legislative and cosmic ……

## what distinguishes the legislative words

the legislative words have distinguishing features. the first is that they are chosen: god, glorified and exalted is he, selects for these words whom he wills of his creation, as he said, exalted is he: {god knows best where to place his message} (sūrat al-anʿām 6:124) — and in the other reading, {god knows best where to place his messages}.

here there is a fine point of inquiry, in the interpretation of his words "his message" (risālatahu) and "his messages" (risālātihi): what is the difference between the two? the answer is that his words "his message" mean the revealed law in its entirety, while his words "his messages" mean the rulings in their multiplicity, for every ruling is a message in its own right — just as you write a letter to someone about a matter you want, then send him another letter, and all of that is called a letter, and the plural of it is letters. in the same way, the angel's descent with a chapter or with verses is called a message, and the revealed law in its entirety is called a message. it is for this reason that the word was made plural at one time and singular at another, and this verse has been read in both ways…
r:
الكلام صفة كمال لله سبحانه وتعالى، والله تعالى تكلم بكلمات تشريعية وكلمات كونية، وكما أنه تعالى يتكلم فهو أيضاً يتصف بالسكوت، ولكنه سكوت عن علم فهو صفة كمال لله تعالى.
كلمات الله الشرعية والكونية:
يقول الشيخ حفظه الله: [ويتكلم متى شاء بما شاء.................... ] التكلم صفة كمال لله عز وجل، وكلامه تعالى شرعي وكوني.......
ميزة الكلمات الشرعية:
والكلمات الشرعية لها ميزات: الميزة الأولى: هي الاختيار لها، فإن الله سبحانه وتعالى يصطفي لهذه الكلمات من شاء من خلقه، كما قال تعالى: اللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ حَيْثُ يَجْعَلُ رِسَالَتَهُ [الأنعام:124] ، في القراءة الأخرى: (اللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ حَيْثُ يَجْعَلُ رسالاته) وهنا بحث دقيق وهو في تفسير قوله: (رسالته) و(رسالاته) ما الفرق بينهما؟ والجواب: أن قوله (رسالته) هي الشريعة بكاملها، وقوله (رسالاته) هي الأحكام على كثرتها، فكل حكم رسالة بخصوصها، مثلما تكتب رسالة إلى شخص في أمر تريده ثم ترسل إليه رسالة أخرى، فكل ذلك يسمى رسالة وتجمع على رسائل، فكذلك نزول الملك بسورة أو بآيات يسمى رسالة، والشريعة بكاملها تسمى رسالة، فلهذا جمعت تارة وأفردت أخرى، وبهما قرئ في هذه الآية...

t: The Names and Attributes Series [10]
a: سلسلة الأسماء والصفات [10]
b:
*[site synopsis]* god, exalted is he, encompasses his creation in knowledge and in overpowering might, and wherever they turn towards him he turns towards them. a person should therefore be mindful of his lord and should comply with his law and his command.

## the mention of the attributes of encompassing, form and face

## affirming god's encompassing of his creation

the sheikh says:

*[he has encompassed mankind; and wherever one turns to face, there is the face of god, majestic is he.]*

this is another attribute, the attribute of encompassing (iḥāṭah), and this attribute amounts to two attributes. the first is the attribute of encompassing in the sense of the perfection of knowledge and apprehension, and this is the meaning of the general accompaniment (al-maʿiyyah al-ʿāmmah). the second is in the sense of overpowering might and compelling dominion.

this encompassing, in the sense of overpowering, divides into two kinds: immediate and deferred. the immediate is god's grievous seizure, with which he seizes those who deny the truth; his grievous seizure with which he seizes them belongs to his encompassing in the sense of his overpowering and his compelling dominion, and so it is an immediate overpowering. as for the deferred, it is his seizing them on the day of resurrection…
r:
الله تعالى محيط بخلقه علماً وقهراً، وحيثما توجهوا إليه أقبل عليهم، فلذلك ينبغي أن يراقب المرء ربه، ويمتثل شرعه وأمره.
ذكر صفات الإحاطة والصورة والوجه.
إثبات إحاطة الله بخلقه:
يقول الشيخ: [أحاط بالناس وأينما يول مستقبل فثم وجه الله جل] هذه صفة أخرى وهي صفة الإحاطة، وهذه الصفة عبارة عن صفتين: الصفة الأولى: صفة الإحاطة بمعنى كمال العلم والإدراك، وهذه هي معنى المعية العامة. والصفة الثانية: بمعنى القهر والجبروت، وهذه الإحاطة التي بمعنى القهر تنقسم إلى قسمين: ناجز ومتأخر. فالناجز منها: هو أخذ الله الوبيل الذي يأخذ به المكذبين، فأخذه الوبيل الذي يأخذهم به هو من إحاطته بمعنى قهره وجبروته، فهو قهر ناجز. وأما المتأخر فهو أخذهم يوم القيامة...

t: The Names and Attributes Series [11]
a: سلسلة الأسماء والصفات [11]
b:
*[site synopsis]* among the greatest of god's attributes are the attribute of rising (istiwāʾ), the attribute of descending to the lowest heaven, and the attribute of highness and aboveness. the people of the sunnah affirm them without likening god to creation and without divesting him of his attributes, while the anthropomorphists and those who divest him of his attributes have gone astray concerning them.

## some of god's active attributes

## affirming the attribute of rising for god, majestic and exalted

the sheikh, may god preserve him, says:

*[he rose towards the heaven, and he rose thereafter over the throne — with a difference in what is contained.]*

this is another attribute, the attribute of rising, and it is one of the active attributes. it is of two kinds: the first, the kind governed by the preposition "towards" (ilā); the second, the kind governed by the preposition "over" (ʿalā).

the first kind, governed by "towards", comes with respect to the heaven, in his words: {then he rose towards the heaven while it was smoke, and said to it and to the earth: come, willingly or unwillingly. they said: we come willingly} (sūrat fuṣṣilat 41:11). rising governed by "towards" has the sense of turning to and regarding. as for rising governed by "over", its meaning is settling and fixity.

as for the rising of god, glorified and exalted is he, over his throne, it is not interpreted. it is one of the established attributes whose recitation is their interpretation, and it is not permissible to interpret it by anything whatever, because we have no knowledge of this. for this reason, whoever interprets it by what we have interpreted rising by in the language has innovated. so whoever says "he rose over the throne" in the sense of "he settled upon it", or anything of that sort, has innovated in the religion of god, for nothing of this has come down from anyone…
r:
من أعظم صفات الله صفة الاستواء وصفة النزول إلى السماء الدنيا، وصفة العلو والفوقية، وأهل السنة يثبتونها بلا تشبيه ولا تعطيل، وقد ضل فيها المشبهة والمعطلة.
من صفات الله الفعلية.
إثبات صفة الاستواء لله جل وعلا:
يقول الشيخ حفظه الله: [قد استوى إلى السماء واستوى بعد على العرش بخلف المحتوى] هذه صفة أخرى هي صفة الاستواء وهي من الصفات الفعلية، وهي على نوعين: النوع الأول: المعدى بإلى، والنوع الثاني: المعدى بعلى فالنوع الأول: المعدى بإلى، جاء في السماء في قوله: ثُمَّ اسْتَوَى إِلَى السَّمَاءِ وَهِيَ دُخَانٌ فَقَالَ لَهَا وَلِلأَرْضِ اِئْتِيَا طَوْعاً أَوْ كَرْهاً قَالَتَا أَتَيْنَا طَائِعِينَ [فصلت:11] والاستواء المعدى بإلى هو بمعنى التوجه والنظر، وأما الاستواء المعدى بعلى فمعناه الاستقرار والثبات. وأما استواء الله سبحانه وتعالى على عرشه فلا يفسر، فهو من الصفات الثابتة التي قراءتها تفسيرها ولا يجوز تفسيرها بأي شيء؛ لأننا لا علم لنا بهذا؛ فلهذا من فسره بما فسرنا به الاستواء في اللغة فقد ابتدع، فمن قال: استوى على العرش بمعنى: استقر عليه أو نحو هذا فقد ابتدع في دين الله، فلم يرد هذا عن أحد...

t: The Names and Attributes Series [12]
a: سلسلة الأسماء والصفات [12]
b:
*[site synopsis]* among the pillars that every muslim is obliged to believe in is belief in the books that god, mighty and majestic, sent down upon his messengers and his prophets — those of them that are named and those that are not — and that the qur'an is the seal of them and abrogates them, and that it is the speech of god, mighty and majestic. and of what must be believed is that the speech of god, mighty and majestic, is one of his attributes: he speaks when he wills, with what he wills, with voice and letter, in which no one of his creation resembles him.

## the obligation (wājib) to believe in the books sent down from god, mighty and majestic

in the name of god, the most merciful, the bestower of mercy. praise belongs to god, lord of the worlds. i invoke blessings and peace upon him who was sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his companions all together. *glory be to you, o god; we have no knowledge except what you have taught us; indeed you are the all-knowing, the all-wise. o god, teach us what benefits us, and benefit us by what you have taught us, and increase us in knowledge, o most merciful of those who show mercy!*

the sheikh, may god preserve him, says:

*[and the books that were sent down upon the messengers of mankind are of his speech, majestic is he — so leave aside their saying that the qur'an points to the speech, or points to that which the speech points to.]*

among the pillars of faith is belief in the revealed books. this pillar, at root, falls within the first pillar, which is belief in god. the pillars of faith are six, but three of them go back to one. for belief in god comprises belief in the revealed books and belief in the decree, because the revealed books are the speech of god, and the decree belongs to god's knowledge; so all of this goes back to belief in god.

thus these divisions come back, in reality, to four: belief in god, belief in the angels, belief in the messengers, and belief in the last day…
r:
من الأركان التي يجب على كل مسلم الإيمان بها: الإيمان بالكتب التي أنزلها الله عز وجل على رسله وأنبيائه، ما سمي منها وما لم يسم، وأن القرآن خاتمها وناسخها، وأنه كلام الله عز وجل. ومما يجب الإيمان به أن كلام الله عز وجل صفة من صفاته، فهو يتكلم متى شاء بما شاء، بصوت وحرف لا يشبهه في ذلك أحد من خلقه.
وجوب الإيمان بالكتب المنزلة من عند الله عز وجل:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين، وأصلي وأسلم على من بعث رحمة للعالمين، وعلى آله وأصحابه أجمعين. سبحانك اللهم لا علم لنا إلا ما علمتنا إنك أنت العليم الحكيم، اللهم علمنا ما ينفعنا، وانفعنا بما علمتنا، وزدنا علماً يا أرحم الراحمين! يقول الشيخ حفظه الله: [والكتب التي على رسل البشر أنزل من كلامه جل فذر قولهم القرآن قد دل على الـ كلام أو على الذي الكلام دل] من أركان الإيمان: الإيمان بالكتب المنزلة، وهذا الركن في أصله داخل في الركن الأول الذي هو الإيمان بالله؛ فأركان الإيمان ستة، لكن ثلاثة منها ترجع إلى واحد. فالإيمان بالله يشمل الإيمان بالكتب المنزلة والإيمان بالقدر؛ لأن الكتب المنزلة كلام الله، والقدر من علم الله، فهذا كله يرجع إلى الإيمان بالله. فإذاً: تعود هذه الأقسام في حقيقتها إلى أربعة: الإيمان بالله، والإيمان بالملائكة، والإيمان بالرسل، والإيمان باليوم الآخر...

t: The Names and Attributes Series [13]
a: سلسلة الأسماء والصفات [13]
b:
*[site synopsis]* to god, exalted is he, belong the most beautiful names and the most exalted attributes. the people of the sunnah have affirmed for god what he affirmed for himself of attributes and names, in the manner that befits his majesty, and they have censured whoever deviates concerning god's names or denies them, and likewise his attributes.

## affirming god's most beautiful names

the sheikh, may god preserve him, said:

*[his most beautiful names point to the attributes, and so the faces of the deniers were humbled ……]*

## the derivation of the word "name"

the word "name" (ism) is disputed. it is said that it is derived from sumuww, elevation, because that which is named is elevated by it, so that it raises it from the condition of being unknown to the condition of being known, and it comes to be known by it. and it is said that it is derived from simah, a mark, because it is a mark upon that which is named.

the kufans and the basrans differed over it. the basrans said: its root is s-m-w, on the pattern of qinw; its final radical was dropped and compensated for by the conjunctive hamzah, as in ibn — for the conjunctive hamzah in that word is a substitute for the final radical, its root being banaw, and so on. the kufans said: its root is w-s-m, from simah, which is the mark; so it is the first radical of the word that was dropped, and the conjunctive hamzah was put in its place.

but the position of the basrans is the sounder, because we say asmāʾ and we do not say awsām; and we say sumayy and we do not say wusaym; and we say "i named my son zayd" (sammaytu) and we do not say "i marked my son zayd" (wasamtu). this is what one of them expressed when he said:

*the basran derived the noun from samā, and the kufan derived it from wasama; and the position given precedence is the manifest one — its evidence is asmāʾ and sumayy.*
r:
لله تعالى الأسماء الحسنى والصفات العلا، وقد أثبت أهل السنة لله ما أثبته لنفسه من الصفات والأسماء كما يليق بجلاله، وذموا من ألحد في أسماء الله أو نفاها، وكذلك صفاته.
إثبات أسماء الله الحسنى.
قال الشيخ حفظه الله: [ أسماؤه الحسنى على الصفات دلت فذلت أوجه النفاة ......].
أصل اشتقاق الاسم:
والاسم مختلف فيه: فقيل: هو مشتق من السمو؛ لأنه يسمو به مسماه فيرفعه من حالة المجهولية إلى المعلومية فيعرف به. وقيل: مشتق من السمة؛ لأنه علامة على مسماه، وقد اختلف الكوفيون والبصريون فيه: فقال البصريون: أصله (سمو) كقنو فحذفت لامه وعرضت الهاء بهمزة الوصل مثل ابن، فإن همزة الوصل التي فيه عوض من اللام وأصله بنو وهكذا. وقال الكوفيون: أصله (وسم) من السمة التي هي العلامة، ففاء الكلمة هي المحذوفة وعوض منها همزة الوصل. لكن مذهب البصريين أصح؛ لأننا نقول: أسماء ولا نقول: أوسام، ونقول: سمي ولا نقول: وُسَيم، ونقول: سميت ابني زيداً، ولا نقول: وسمت ابني زيداً ، وهذا الذي يقول فيه أحدهم: اشتق الاسم من سما البصريُ واشتقه من وسم الكوفـيُ والمذهب المقدم الجليّ دليله الأسماء والـسـميُّ

t: The Names and Attributes Series [14]
a: سلسلة الأسماء والصفات [14]
b:
## why kalālah is called by this name

**question:** why is the inheritance of kalālah called by this name?

**answer:** kalālah is from kalla, meaning to grow weary. a person who has neither ascendant nor descendant is as though he had grown weary of life and so was cut off alone. one says: the horse kalla, when it runs until it gives out; and the sword kalla, when it no longer cuts; and the man kalla, meaning that he grew weary from his journeying. from here comes the derivation of kalālah……

## the meaning of "ear" in his words, exalted is he: {and they say, "he is an ear." say: "an ear of good for you"}

**question:** god, exalted is he, said: {and they say, "he is an ear." say: "an ear of good for you"} (sūrat al-tawbah 9:61). does "ear" here mean listening?

**answer:** no — because the verse has been read with two of the seven canonical readings (qirāʾāt): "say: an ear (udhn) of good for you", with the vowelless letter; and it has been read "say: an ear (udhun) of good for you" (sūrat al-tawbah 9:61), with the ḍammah. the meaning in both is: one who conveys.

for "the ear" among the arabs is the funnel through which milk is poured into the milk vessel, and what is meant by it is that which conveys. when the hypocrites were asked to honour the messenger of god, may god bless him and grant him peace, they would say: "he is nothing but an ear" — that is, one who merely conveys from god — as though he were in the position of the funnel into which the milk is poured, and which then has no further use after that. so god answered this saying of theirs with his words: {say: an ear of good for you. he believes in god, and has faith in the believers, and is a mercy to those of you who believe} (sūrat al-tawbah 9:61)…
r:
سبب تسمية الكلالة بهذه التسمية.
السؤال: لماذا سمي ميراث الكلالة بهذا الاسم؟ الجواب: أن الكلالة من (كلَّ) بمعنى تعب، والإنسان الذي ليس له أصل ولا فرع كأنه قد تعب من الحياة فانقطع وحده، ويقال: كلَّ الفرس إذا جرى حتى انقطع، وكلَّ السيف إذا لم يقطع، وكلَّ الإنسان بمعنى: تعب من سيره، فمن هنا جاء اشتقاق الكلالة.......
معنى الأذن في قوله تعالى: (ويقولون هو أذن قل أذن خير لكم):
السؤال: قال تعالى: وَيَقُولُونَ هُوَ أُذُنٌ قُلْ أُذُنُ خَيْرٍ لَكُمْ [التوبة:61] ، هل (أذن) هنا بمعنى: الاستماع؟.
الجواب: لا؛ لأن الآية قرئت بقراءتين سبعيتين: (قُلْ أُذْنُ خَيْرٍ لَكُمْ) بالإسكان، وقرئت: (قُلْ أُذُنُ خَيْرٍ لَكُمْ)[التوبة:61]، بالضم، والمعنى في كلتيهما أي: موصل، فالأذن عند العرب هو المحقن الذي يحقن به اللبن في وعاء اللبن، والمقصود به: ما يبلغ، فقد كان المنافقون إذا طلب منهم تعظيم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقولون: ما هو إلا أذن، أي: مبلغ عن الله فقط، فكأنه بمثابة المحقن الذي يحقن فيه اللبن، ثم لا يكون له فائدة بعد ذلك، فرد الله عليهم هذا القول بقوله: قُلْ أُذُنُ خَيْرٍ لَكُمْ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَيُؤْمِنُ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَرَحْمَةٌ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مِنْكُمْ [التوبة:61]...

t: Sheikh al-Dedew, President of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars, Lectures in Kuwait on the Role of the Expatriate in Serving the Homeland
a: الشيخ الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء يحاضر في الكويت عن دور المغترب في خدمة الأوطان
b:
his eminence sheikh muhammad al-hasan al-dedew, president of the centre for the formation of scholars, delivered a lecture in kuwait entitled "the role of emigrant communities in serving their homelands", organised by the league of the mauritanian community in kuwait at the kuwait continental hotel, on 18/05/2011.

in his talk the sheikh addressed the opportunities available to a person in this world, and the necessity of using this short lifespan in beneficial knowledge and in lawful earning.

the sheikh said that god, exalted is he, has decreed migrations in the earth upon the children of man. among these migrations are those undertaken in search of knowledge and of provision, and among them are migrations of flight from straitness and distress and in search of freedom.

the sheikh went on at some length in mentioning patterns and examples of these migrations, taking guidance from the migrations of the prophets, peace be upon them, and from examples among the shinqiti emigrants.

in his lecture the sheikh concentrated on directing the community towards the praiseworthy character an emigrant ought to display, and the effective role he undertakes in serving his homeland materially and morally. he also urged the community to be a good embassy for its homeland in knowledge and in character.

the sheikh warned against the passivity and ossification that afflicts some communities, such that they cut themselves off from the mother country and do not integrate into the new society, and so become unsteady in their belonging and in their representation.

the sheikh called upon those living abroad and upon emigrants to keep their bond with the homeland and to serve it by every available means, and called upon them likewise to develop themselves and to make use of the expertise and the experience that contact with others affords, so as to contribute to reforming their homelands and to raising the awareness of their societies.

poetry and letters had their presence, despite the shortness of the time, as the poets did not let slip the opportunity to welcome the sheikh and to acclaim his standing and his contributions in calling people to islam, in scholarship and in reform.

the lecture [drew] a notable attendance from members of the community, and some guests from among the kuwaiti brethren also attended.

at the end of the lecture a shield of appreciation was presented to the sheikh by the league of the mauritanian community, for the great roles his eminence undertakes in making the country's culture known and in representing it in scholarly gatherings.

the lecture was organised by the league of the mauritanian community in kuwait, as part of scholarly and cultural activities the league holds in order to activate the bridge of communication among the community itself on the one hand, and between them and their homeland on the other.
r:
ألقى فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء محاضرة في الكويت بعنوان: " دور الجاليات المهاجرة في خدمة الأوطان" نظمتها رابطة الجالية الموريتانية بالكويت وذلك بفندق " كويت كونتينانتال"، بتاريخ: 18/05/2011.
تطرق الشيخ في حديثه إلى الفرص المتاحة للإنسان في هذه الدنيا، وضرورة استغلال هذا العمر القصير في العلوم النافعة والكسب الحلال.
وقال الشيخ إن الله تعالى قد كتب على بني البشر الهجرات في الأرض؛ ومن هذه الهجرات ما يكون طلبا للعلم والرزق، ومنها ما يكون هجرة هرب من الضيق والحرج وطلب للحرية.
وقد استطرد الشيخ في ذكر النماذج والأمثلة على هذه الهجرات، مسترشدا بهجرة الأنبياء عليهم السلام، ونماذج من المهاجرين الشناقطة.
وركز الشيخ في محاضرته على التوجيه للجالية لما ينبغي أن يتحلى به المهاجر من أخلاق حميدة، وما يضطلع به من دور فعال في خدمة وطنه ماديا ومعنويا، كما حث الجالية على أن تكون سفارة حسنة لوطنها في العلم والأخلاق.
وحذر الشيخ من السلبية والتكلس الذي يصيب بعض الجاليات بحيث تنفصل عن الوطن الأم ولا تندمج مع المجتمع الجديد وبذلك تصبح متذبذبة في انتمائها وتمثيلها.
ودعا الشيخ المغتربين والمهاجرين إلى الارتباط بالوطن وخدمته بكل السبل المتاحة كما دعاهم إلى تطوير أنفسهم واستغلال الخبرات والتجارب التي يتيحها التواصل مع الآخر من أجل الإسهام في إصلاح أوطانهم وتوعية مجتمعاتهم.
وقد كان للشعر والأدب حضوره رغم ضيق الوقت حيث لم يفوت الشعراء فرصة الترحيب بالشيخ والإشادة بمكانته وإسهاماته الدعوية والعلمية والإصلاحية.
وقد شهت المحاضرة حضورا بارزا من أفراد الجالية، كما حضرها بعض الضيوف من الأشقاء الكويتيين.
وفي نهاية المحاضرة تم إهداء درع تقديري للشيخ من طرف رابطة الجالية الموريتانية على الأدوار الكبيرة التي يضطلع بها فضيلته في التعريف بثقافة البلد وتمثيله في المحافل العلمية.
وقد نظمت المحاضرة من طرف رابطة الجالية الموريتانية في الكويت، ضمن أنشطة علمية وثقافية تقيمها الرابطة من أجل تفعيل جسر التواصل بين الجالية نفسها من جهة، وبينهم مع وطنهم من جهة أخرى.
لمتابعة المحاضرة اضغط هنا

t: Sheikh al-Dedew Presides over the Ḥudāʾ al-Ṣaḥrāʾ Festival of Literature and Chant in the Capital, Nouakchott
a: الشيخ الددو يترأس فعاليات مهرجان حداء الصحراء للأدب والنشيد في العاصمة نواكشوط.
b:
his eminence the erudite sheikh muhammad al-hasan al-dedew, president of the centre for the formation of scholars and president of the future association, presided over the ḥudāʾ al-ṣaḥrāʾ festival of literature and chant, organised by the future association for calling to islam, culture and education in the period from 26/05 to 28/05/2011 at the olympic complex in tevragh zeina, on each evening of the festival, alongside morning lectures and panels at the premises of the old youth house.

in his address during the opening session of the ḥudāʾ al-ṣaḥrāʾ festival, the sheikh said that this festival came as an attempt to meet the wishes of young people, and as the future association's message to them, at their various ages, in caring for this important segment among the strata of the community.

his eminence the sheikh added that whoever travels the path of god and the sunnah of his messenger muhammad, may god bless him and grant him peace, passes through dangerous slippages and difficult stages, and must have a driving-song (ḥudāʾ) to gladden his heart and to help him hold to the straight road — exactly as the driving-song helps camels to keep marching in the noonday heat; and it is part of the natural disposition (fiṭrah) upon which god created people.

sheikh al-dedew said that the ḥudāʾ meant in the festival is not the ḥudāʾ of the voice, and the desert is not a particular desert; rather the real desert is the road of life, and the ḥudāʾ is whatever stirs resolve and helps one hold to the straight road.

the sheikh affirmed that the future association for calling to islam, culture and education had needed, in its travelling on the path of god and his messenger, a "ḥudāʾ" to keep it company on that blessed journey; and for that reason — the erudite al-dedew, may god preserve him, adds — its first festival was connected with the first word of its name, which is calling to islam, and the second with the second word, which is culture; and he affirmed that the third would be about education, which is the last word in the association's name.

in the second axis of the first session of the morning programme at the youth house, sheikh al-dedew said in his intervention: "whoever is not moved by a beautiful voice is corrupt in temperament and in nature, and the controls the revealed law sets in these matters cannot be overstepped." he mentioned that the majority of the people of knowledge hold that chant, if it is joined to stringed instruments or contains what impugns the honour of muslims, is forbidden (ḥarām), and that what is other than that is permissible (mubāḥ); and that the accommodating revealed law came to raise and to refine human natures. the sheikh went on to give examples of this. then the sheikh answered the doubts that had been raised about the previous evening — that there had been the sounds of wind instruments in it — by saying that what had been heard was only natural human voices to which processing had been applied.

at the close of the second session of the morning programme at the youth house — and after lectures by a number of writers and poets from various arab countries, alongside mauritanian writers — the sheikh followed with a closing word in this session, in which he treated an aspect of hassaniya literature, acclaiming the creativity of the hassaniya poets, even in their blending of hassaniya literature with the knowledge of jurisprudence and of legal theory (uṣūl al-fiqh) — in an indication from him that knowledge of the revealed sciences was among the literary patterns prevailing in mauritanian society.

## close of the festival

sheikh al-dedew closed the ḥudāʾ al-ṣaḥrāʾ festival on its fourth evening at one o'clock after midnight on the night of saturday. at the close of the festival sheikh al-dedew renewed his thanks to the president of the republic and his government for the efforts they had made in bringing such purposeful activities to success. he also thanked the officials and diplomats who attended, singling out among them the jordanian and the egyptian ambassadors.

he likewise renewed his thanks to the sheikhs and to the young men and young women, and wished them guidance and success. he also thanked the guests, who he said had come from distant lands seeking nothing but the face of god, and gave the audience the good news that the chanter abu ratib would be making visits in the interior of the country.

the sheikh thanked the organising committees, which he said had reached twenty in number. he also thanked the businessmen who took part in financing this festival, and the police who kept watch over security during these days; and he promised the audience a repetition of such activities in the coming years. he then closed with a supplication for those responsible for the country and those supervising this activity, for those running the future association, for the chanters and the poets and all those present, and for the muslims generally.
r:
ترأس فضيلة العلامة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء ورئيس جمعية المستقبل مهرجان حداء الصحراء للأدب والنشيد الذي تنظمه جمعية المستقبل للدعوة والثقافة والتعليم في الفترة من 26/05 إلى 28/05/2011 بالمركب الأولمبي بتفرغ زينة مساء كل يوم من أيام المهرجان، إلى جانب محاضرات وندوات صباحية بمقر دار الشباب القديمة.
وقال الشيخ في كلمته خلال الجلسة الافتتاحية لمهرجان حداء الصحراء إن هذا المهرجان جاء محاولة لتحقيق رغبات الشباب ورسالة جمعية المستقبل إلىهم بمختلف أعمارهم، للعناية بهذه الفئة الهامة من شرائح الأمة.
وأضاف فضيلة الشيخ أن السائر علي طريق الله وسنة رسوله محمد صلي الله عليه وسلم يمر بمنزلقات خطيرة ومراحل صعبة، لا بد له من حداء يسر وجدانه ويعين على الاستقامة على الطريق، تماما كما يعين الحداء الإبل على مواصلة السير في الهاجرة ،وهو من فطرة الله التي فطر الناس عليها.
وقال الشيخ الددو إن الحداء المقصود في المهرجان ليس حداء الصوت، والصحراء ليست صحراء معينة، وإنما الصحراء الحقيقية هي الطريق في الحياة والحداء هو ما يحرك الهمم، ويعين على الاستقامة على الطريق.
وأكد الشيخ أن جمعية المستقبل للدعوة والثقافة والتعليم احتاجت في سيرها علي طريق الله ورسوله إلي "حداء" يؤنسها في تلك الرحلة الميمونة، ولذلك ـ يضيف العلامة الددو حفظه الله ـ كان أول مهرجان لها متعلق بالكلمة الأولي من اسمها وهي الدعوة والثاني بالكلمة الثانية وهي الثقافة، مؤكدا علي أن يكون الثالث عن التعليم وهو الكلمة الأخيرة من اسم الجمعية.
وفي المحور الثاني من الجلسة الأولى من البرنامج الصباحي بدار الشباب قال الشيخ الددو في مداخلته: "إن من لا يحركه الصوت الحسن فاسد المزاج والطبع، وأن ضوابط الشرع في هذه الأمور لا يمكن تجاوزها.."، وذكر أن جمهور أهل العلم على أن النشيد إذا كان مرتبطا بأوتار أو فيه ما يسيء لأعراض المسلمين كان حراما، وما سوى ذلك مباح، وأن الشريعة السمحة جاءت للرقي بطباع البشر وتهذيبها واستطرد الشيخ أمثلة على ذلك، ثم رد الشيخ على الشكوك التي أثيرت حول الأمسية السابقة من أنها كانت فيها أصوات مزامير بقوله: إن ما سمع إنما هو أصوات بشرية طبيعة أجريت عليها معالجة.
وفي ختام الجلسة الثانية من البرنامج الصباحي بدار الشباب – وبعد محاضرات لعدد من الأدباء والشعراء من دول عربية مختلفة إلى جانب أدباء موريتانيين – عقّب الشيخ بكلمة ختامية في هذه الجلسة تناول فيها جانبا من الأدب الحساني مشيدا بإبداع الشعراء الحسانيين حتى في مزجهم بين الأدب الحساني والمعارف الفقهية والأصولية في إشارة منه إلى أن معرفة العلوم الشرعية كانت ضمن الأنماط الأدبية السائدة في المجتمع الموريتاني.
ختام المهرجان:
اختتم الشيخ الددو مهرجان حُداء الصحراء في أمسيته الرابعة في الساعة الواحدة بعد منتصف ليلة السبت، حيث جدد الشيخ الددو شكره في ختام المهرجان لرئيس الجمهورية وحكومته على الجهود التي بذلوها في إنجاح مثل هذه المناشط الهادفة، كما شكر الرسميين والدبلوماسيين الذين حضروا وخصص من بينهم السفيرين الأردني والمصري.
وجدد شكره كذلك للشيوخ والشباب والشابات وتمنى لهم الهداية والتوفيق، كما شكر الضيوف الذين قال إنهم جاءوا من بلاد بعيدة لا يريدون إلا وجه الله وبشر الجمهور بأن المنشد أبو راتب سوف تكون له زيارات في الداخل.
وشكر الشيخ اللجان المنظمة التي قال إنها بلغت عشرين لجنة، كما شكر رجال الأعمال الذين شاركوا في تمويل هذا المهرجان، رجال الشرطة الذين سهروا على الأمن هذه الأيام، ووعد الجمهور بتكرار مثل هذه المناشط في السنوات القادمة، ثم ختم بالدعاء للقائمين على البلد والمشرفين على هذا النشاط، والقائمين على جمعية المستقبل والمنشدين والشعراء وسائر الحضور والمسلمين عامة.

t: Replies to Questions Sent to the Site, Part 2
a: ردود على الأسئلة الواردة للموقع ج2
b:
**question:** what is the ruling on studying on a scholarship to australia, given that i tried to complete my studies in my own country and was not able to, and my specialisation is computing?

**answer:** praise belongs to god, lord of the worlds. to proceed: the ruling on studying abroad on a scholarship, anywhere in the world, takes on whichever of the rulings applies according to the intention of the one who does it. if the one who does it intends by it to raise the standing of this community and to serve it, and to discharge the communally obligatory duties (furūḍ al-kifāyāt), then he is one striving in the path of god by his study and his scholarship, and he is rewarded for everything that befalls him and for all the time he spends outside his country. the prophet, may god bless him and grant him peace, sent zayd ibn thabit al-ansari to the jews to learn their language, on a mission of that kind, and that is the basis of the permissibility of studying abroad on a scholarship.

but a person must know the rulings that govern studying abroad, and must prepare for it, for he is exposed to many trials. he must know the rulings on the dispensations (rukhaṣ) in what concerns the prayer and the fast, and he must know also the rulings on mixing with women who are not close relatives (ajnabiyyāt) and on looking at them, for he is exposed to great trials, and so he must be careful in this. in addition, he must also be careful, in the place of his study, that there be near him a mosque or an islamic centre in which he may attend the friday prayer and the congregational prayers together with the muslims. for any city in which there is no mosque for the muslims — residence in it is not lawful except under compulsion.

the compilers of the sunan collections reported that the prophet, may god bless him and grant him peace, said: "i am quit of every muslim who resides among the idolaters, such that their two fires are not visible to one another." that is where he is alone, with no muslim with him, so that if he were to die there would be one to attend him, to prepare his body and to bury him. but as for one who is in a country in which there are muslims who are able to establish the rites — al-hafiz ibn hajar mentioned in al-fatḥ, from al-mawardi, that a country becomes an abode of islam by the presence of muslims in it.

**question:** what is called in hassaniya *aṭlayṣah*: a man who lends money to people. you come to him wanting, say, a million ouguiya. he says to you: i will give you the million for a million three hundred, and you agree to that. he goes with you to the market and buys you goods for the very same million that is in his pocket, and hands the goods over to you, and you sell them to someone else for less than that price; and after a year you give him a million three hundred in cash.

is it permissible for me to take cash in this way??

**answer:** no. this is one of the stratagems used to reach usurious gain (ribā), and the messenger of god, may god bless him and grant him peace, forbade them. he said that when god forbids a thing he forbids its price: "god cursed the jews — god forbade them the fats, and they rendered them down and sold them and consumed their price." for this reason a person must beware of usurious gain and of everything that comes near it. the messenger of god, may god bless him and grant him peace, cursed the one who consumes usurious gain, the one who pays it, the one who records it and its two witnesses, and said: they are alike.

likewise the messenger of god, may god bless him and grant him peace, made plain the prohibition of these stratagems. when a man came to him bringing dates from khaybar — janīb dates, which are the best kind of dates — he said to him: "are all the dates of khaybar like this?" he said: "no; we sell one measure of janīb for two measures of the mixed sort, the jamʿ." he said: "do not do so. that is ribāʾ" — that is, usurious gain — "sell the jamʿ for dirhams, then buy janīb with the dirhams."

and it has come down from him, in the musnad of imam ahmad and the mustadrak of al-hakim, that he said: "one single dirham of usurious gain that a man consumes is graver than thirty-six acts of fornication." god, exalted is he, has forbidden usurious gain and made plain its harm in the hereafter. he said, exalted is he: {those who consume usury will not stand except as one stands whom satan has prostrated by his touch. that is because they said: trade is only like usury. but god has permitted trade and has forbidden usury. so whoever receives an admonition from his lord and desists, he may keep what is past, and his affair rests with god; but whoever returns — those are the companions of the fire, in which they abide for ever. (275) god blights usury and causes acts of charity to grow, and god does not love any ungrateful sinner. (276) indeed those who believe and do righteous deeds and establish the prayer and give the zakat — they have their reward with their lord, and no fear shall come upon them, nor shall they grieve. (277) o you who believe, be mindful of god and give up what remains of usury, if you are believers. (278) and if you do not, then be notified of a war from god and his messenger. but if you repent, you may have your principal sums — you neither wrong nor are wronged. (279)} (sūrat al-baqarah 2:275-279).

so a person must repent of this transaction and must not embark upon it thereafter; and if he has already embarked upon it, let him repent. the repentance of the one who consumes usurious gain differs from the repentance of the one who pays it. the one who pays it is obliged, in his repentance, to do no more than seek forgiveness, and to intend not to return to it, and to resolve upon that, and to feel remorse for what he neglected of his duty towards god. as for the one who consumes usurious gain, he is obliged to return with repentance and remorse, and to give back what he took of usurious gain and so rid himself of it: if he knows whose it is he returns it to him, and otherwise he gives it away in charity, so that he has rid himself of it — and in that case it is not by way of voluntary charity (ṣadaqah) but by way of repentance.

**question:** is it permissible to kiss one's paternal aunt and one's maternal aunt on the cheeks, as is the custom of people in algeria?

**answer:** if she is advanced in years, and this is the custom of the people of the country, and it does not stir desire in the person, and it is by way of affection, then there is no harm in it, and it does not break the ablution. if it is otherwise, then it is not lawful for a person to embark upon it — as with one who feels desire stirred by it. the same applies to kissing the hands and the head: it takes on whichever of these rulings applies, and is judged according to the difference of circumstances.

as for women who are not close relatives, it is not lawful to approach them at all, nor to touch them — so how much less to extend this to them? some people suppose that the wife of one's maternal uncle is like one's maternal aunt, or like one's paternal aunt; and this is not correct. the wife of the maternal uncle is not a close relative, and the wife of the paternal uncle is not a close relative, and it is not lawful for a person to treat her as he treats his maternal aunt or his paternal aunt.

**question:** i am a muslim student in one of the western countries. i have heard from some colleagues, reported from the sheikh, that he gives the opinion that combining prayers is permissible without travel and without illness in the case of muslim students in the west, especially where there is fear that the time will be lost, in the case of the prayers that share a time. and i have read on some islamic websites on the internet that combining the friday prayer with the afternoon prayer is forbidden. to make my situation clear: we have a single hour that is supposed to be the lunch break, and after it we are obliged to return to class, and sometimes we continue in class until about an hour after sunset, or near to that, with the times changing according to the seasons. so we are compelled to use this hour to go to the mosque for the friday prayer, and if we do not pray the afternoon prayer in combination with it, it will be all but impossible for us to pray it before sunset and the passing of its time.

**answer:** combining two prayers on account of work is permissible, on the stronger position. it is established in the two ṣaḥīḥ collections that the prophet, may god bless him and grant him peace, combined the noon prayer and the afternoon prayer, and the sunset prayer and the night prayer, and prayed them as eight and as seven, in medina, without fear and without rain — that is from the hadith of ibn abbas. and in ṣaḥīḥ muslim it is reported that he was asked: and why? he said: he wished not to place his community in difficulty. so where the difficulty is actually present — as in the loss of the prayer's time — a person should combine.

this is in cases other than the friday prayer, for all the prayers, such as the noon prayer and the two evening prayers, have come down as being combined for one reason or another. a person may combine the two noon-period prayers at the beginning of the time of the noon prayer, or at the end of the time of the afternoon prayer, if he is compelled to that on account of work; but it is not permissible for this to become a habit with him, and he is not to do it without necessity (ḍarūrah). likewise, if he is able, he should combine the two noon-period prayers at the end of the afternoon prayer's time, or the two evening prayers at the end of the night prayer's time. of the two forms of combining, the better is the one that is the easier. but this ought not to become a habit that a person adopts permanently; rather he does it in a case of necessity, and of general need (ḥājah) that stands in the place of necessity.

as for combining the friday prayer with the afternoon prayer, there is disagreement in it. some of the people of knowledge held that the friday prayer is the obligation of its own day and is not a noon prayer, and this is a well-known transmitted report in the hanbali school. it entails that the time of the friday prayer and the time of the noon prayer are different, for they hold that the time of the friday prayer enters a little before the sun's decline; and on that basis it is not combined with the afternoon prayer, because it does not share a time with it and is not like the noon prayer. the other transmitted report, which is the position of the majority, is that the friday prayer is a shortened noon prayer and its time is the time of the noon prayer; and therefore a person is able to combine the afternoon prayer with it. this is what we give as our opinion, in order to lift necessity, and the need that stands in its place, when a person is compelled to it and the alternative is the loss of the prayer's time. he says, exalted is he: {indeed the prayer has been for the believers a prescription at fixed times} (sūrat al-nisāʾ 4:103).

the basis of combining is established by what we have mentioned of the sound reports from the prophet, may god bless him and grant him peace. it has six causes, which are the ones stated explicitly in the books of jurisprudence:

**the first cause:** the standing at arafat, for which the two noon-period prayers are combined by bringing the later one forward.

**the second cause:** the halting at muzdalifah, for which the two evening prayers are combined by delaying the earlier one.

**the third cause:** travel. the prophet, may god bless him and grant him peace, used to combine the two noon-period prayers and the two evening prayers while travelling. there has been disagreement about this: whether it is a condition that one be actually pressing on in the journey, or that this is not a condition for it, or that the condition is that a person be in the state of travel.

malik reported in the muwaṭṭaʾ that the prophet, may god bless him and grant him peace, was at tabuk, and he would come out and pray the two noon-period prayers, then go in and not come out again until he came out for the sunset prayer, and would pray the two evening prayers. this is evidence for the permissibility of combining without pressing on in the journey, and without a person's being in an earnest or purposeful journey. for the prophet, may god bless him and grant him peace, was a traveller at tabuk, yet he stayed there twenty-nine days shortening the prayer; and that was because every day he was expecting a surprise attack by the enemy and an invasion by the byzantines, so that every day he was making ready for battle, and for that reason he did not pray the full prayer — even though whoever intends [a residence of] four days in a place he will not leave has thereby dissolved his state of travel, on account of what malik reported in the muwaṭṭaʾ from saʿid ibn al-musayyab: "if you intend a residence of four full days, your state of travel is dissolved"; and on account of what is established in the ṣaḥīḥ from the prophet, may god bless him and grant him peace, who said: "the emigrant may stay in mecca three days after the completion of his rites." what is meant is that residence in mecca was not lawful for the emigrants, but the messenger of god, may god bless him and grant him peace, permitted them to stay in mecca for three days with their nights. that indicates that a residence of three days does not cut off the ruling of travel and is not counted as residence, and that what exceeds it does cut off the ruling of travel. this is the position of the people of careful verification on this question. there are other positions in it, and a clashing among the evidences; but all those evidences, when they are looked at, admit of constructions that may be placed upon them — such as the prophet's staying in mecca seventeen days at its conquest, for on each day he was demolishing an idol and making ready for the war with hawazin and for the campaign against al-taʾif, and he did not intend residence, and residence in mecca was not lawful. and likewise the staying of abd allah ibn umar in azerbaijan, shortening the prayer for six months: for every day he was waiting for the snow to break, and the snow breaks suddenly, with no fixed rule and no regularity, so he was waiting for it to break in order to depart, and for that reason he remained upon shortening.

so whoever is on a journey and comes to a place where he has work, and does not know when his work will end, remains upon his shortening even if he stays there a year waiting for that work; if he was not expecting that, and was every day expecting to leave, then he counts as a traveller journeying in the earth until he departs. and whoever fears that the time will pass must take the dispensations, and these positions we have mentioned and the evidences we have adduced, and by that he is saved, god willing. but this ought not to become a habit with him, for god, exalted is he, fixed the times of the prayer and said: {indeed the prayer has been for the believers a prescription at fixed times}. and it is established from the messenger of god, may god bless him and grant him peace, that he urged the performance of the prayer in its time, in his words, may god bless him and grant him peace, that "the one who misses the afternoon prayer is as though he had been bereft of his family and his wealth"; and as in his words, may god bless him and grant him peace: "whoever prays the two cool prayers enters the garden."

**question:** we are bound by insurance contracts imposed upon us, insuring housing, health and other things, and we pay substantial sums for them without return over a long period, unless we are exposed to something that obliges those insuring companies to compensate us for it — such as a water leak in the house, or a fire, or an illness, and the like. the question is about the permissibility of making a claim, or of exaggerating the losses, with a view to obtaining a larger compensation in one of these cases; and whether that counts as forbidden deceit — bearing in mind that what we pay is more than what we obtain in the supposed compensation.

and what is the ruling on the money reaped in such cases, if it is in fact unlawful money? and what is a muslim obliged to do with it? and is it permissible to return it to those companies? we want your view on that; may god reward you well.

**answer:** a person may resort to a stratagem in order to take what is his. the prophet, may god bless him and grant him peace, permitted al-hajjaj ibn ilat al-sulami, may god be pleased with him, to lie to quraysh in order to take his property from them, at the time of the campaign of khaybar. so it is permissible for a person, if he knows that the compensation is equal to the money that was taken from him, or less than it, to resort to a stratagem for that, even by lying; and that is not called deceit. but if he takes more than the money he paid, he does not return it to the company, because its liability is wholly encumbered (mustaghraqat al-dhimmah) and its money is unlawful; yet he does not take ownership of it himself — rather he spends it in avenues of good, as by paying it to islamic associations working in calling people to islam and in charitable work, and the like. of this same kind is exaggerating in the statement of the damages he has suffered: he may exaggerate until he reaches the limit of what was taken from him, so as to recover the money that was taken from him; and whatever exceeds that, it is not lawful for him to take ownership of it, nor to return it to the company if he has taken it — rather he spends it in avenues of good, as we have mentioned.
